Proposed MOA: metabolic alkalosis, sustained respiratory depression, Bohr-effect hypoxia, inadequate erythrocytosis/failure of erythrocyte release in mice, increased platelet and megakaryocyte counts in mice, macrophage/erythrophage accumulation, increased hemosiderin and oxidative stress driving endothelial tumor induction. Studies in mice provided evidence of bronchioalveolar adenoma and combined adenoma/carcinoma, but the data were inconclusive. The pHG is calculated treating alachlor as a carcinogen using the non-linear approach.

PHG was calculated treating alachlor as a carcinogen via a non-linear approach (point of departure 0.5 mg kg-1 day-1, UF 1000, RSC 20%, 70 kg BW, 2 l day-1 water consumption), yielding a PHG of 4 ppb.

raw_record.support_text: In a case-control study of endometrial cancer in women treated for breast cancer, women who had ever used both tamoxifen and estrogen replacement therapy (ERT) were at substantially increased risk of endometrial cancer (OR = 3.53; 95% CI = 2.15–5.78), while those who used only ERT had a 60% increased risk (OR = 1.62) and tamoxifen-only users showed no significantly elevated risk (OR = 1.14; 95% CI = 0.73–1.81). raw_record.support_text: In this cohort study of workers at a Montana copper smelter (follow-up 1938-1989), relative risks of respiratory cancer death increased with higher cumulative airborne arsenic exposure indices. Relative risks were consistent with a linear excess-relative-risk model (ERR/(mg/m3-year) = 0.21, 95% CI 0.10-0.46), and the authors conclude that the exposure-response comparison provides further support for a linear association between inhaled arsenic exposure and respiratory cancer.

raw_record.extra_details: Analyses adjusted for sulphur dioxide; within each sulphur dioxide category relative risks increased with arsenic exposure, whereas relative risks did not increase with sulphur dioxide exposure within arsenic-exposure categories. ERR/year for light, medium, and heavy exposure categories were 0.04, 0.07, and 0.13, with ratios matching mean airborne arsenic measurements. Curvature in the ERR at lambda=1.0 was attributed to heavy-exposure weighting. Significant dose-response trends (p<0.005) across all tables.

Histopathology showed that uterine tumors (endometrial polyps and stromal sarcomas) and lung adenomas were induced in both genotypes, with the incidence significantly higher in p53(+/-) mice (94% and 81%) than in p53(+/+) mice (37% and 42%). The results suggest female p53(+/-) CBA mice are highly susceptible to ENU-induced uterine carcinogenesis.

raw_record.support_text: Benzene is a cause of human leukemia. The analysis demonstrated that the increased relative risk of leukemia following exposure to benzene varies with time, using a case-control design that compared exposures of cases and matched control subjects in time windows prior to the death of the cases.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: case-control study of subjects with leukemia and matched controls
raw_record.extra_details: Exposure-effect modeling used a backward-time case-control analysis with time-window exposures (E1-4 through E25-29); the Biological Exposure Index (BEI) weighted exposures in the previous 20 years (BEI = 0.011 x E1-4 + 0.0098 x E5-9 + 0.0067 x E10-14 + 0.0012 x E15-19). Cumulative exposure model gave beta = 0.0028. BEI and BEI-squared models both provided highly significant fits (AIC 124.0 for linear-quadratic) surpassing cumulative exposure (AIC 131.1) and the six-time-window model (AIC 130.5). Coefficients for exposures 20 or more years before death were small and negative and treated as noise.

raw_record.support_text: An epidemiologic risk assessment of benzene workers at three plants manufacturing rubber film (rubber hydrochloride) found that the standardized mortality ratio (SMR) for leukemia was 337 (95% CI: 154-641), and SMRs for leukemia rose from 109 to 6637 with increasing cumulative benzene exposure (from <40 ppm-years to >=400 ppm-years). The author interprets the leukemia risk as varying with time after exposure, similar to ionizing radiation, implying benzene exposure is causally related to leukemia mortality.

raw_record.support_text: The Hras128 rat is highly susceptible to mammary carcinogenesis induced by N-methyl-N-nitrosourea (MNU). All Hras128 rats rapidly developed multiple and large mammary carcinomas within 8 weeks after MNU injection, whereas wild-type rats had no or only small carcinomas; wild-type rats showed codon 12 mutations in 28.6% of their mammary carcinomas. Mutation analysis of bladder tumors indicated that the presence of the human c-Ha-ras gene enhances mammary and bladder carcinogenesis.
raw_record.extra_details: Described as inducing 'mammary carcinogenesis'; rapid development of multiple, large mammary carcinomas within 8 weeks in Hras128 rats. Tumors showed codon 12 c-Ha-ras mutations. Susceptibility is enhanced by human c-Ha-ras transgene overexpression.

All cases were diagnosed in stage I, except for one case in the placebo group, which was diagnosed in stage IV.

raw_record.extra_details: Tamoxifen also reduced invasive breast cancer risk by 49% and noninvasive breast cancer by 50% (chemopreventive effect, excluded from scope); in BCPT there were 37 versus 18 endometrial cancer cases (tamoxifen vs placebo), and in the UK trial 4 versus 1. Thromboembolic events, strokes, hot flashes, and gynecologic complaints were more frequent in the tamoxifen group.

raw_record.support_text: Pour and coworkers systematically evaluated the carcinogenicity of nitrosamines and identified N-nitrosobis(2-oxopropyl)amine (BOP) as the most potent and selective pancreatic carcinogen in the Syrian golden hamster model. Given by a single subcutaneous injection, BOP reaches the pancreas via the blood and requires metabolism to an alkylating species that is mutagenic and initiates a carcinogenic sequence. Invasive pancreatic adenocarcinomas emerge in 80-100% of the animals, with tumor latency as short as 8 weeks.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Single subcutaneous injection; invasive pancreatic adenocarcinomas in 80-100% of animals with latency as short as 8 weeks.
raw_record.extra_details: BOP also induces tumors in lung, liver, gallbladder, and kidney. Requires metabolic activation to a mutagenic alkylating species that initiates the carcinogenic sequence. Described as the most potent and selective pancreatic carcinogen in the hamster model.

raw_record.support_text: The best characterized rat pancreatic cancer model was described by Longnecker et al. and involves treating Lewis rats with azaserine, an antimetabolite that induces DNA damage and inhibits DNA synthesis in the rat pancreas but also induces tumors at several other sites, including kidney, breast, and skin. Pancreatic carcinomas were induced by intraperitoneal injection of 150-260 mg/kg azaserine divided into 5-26 weekly doses. The incidence of carcinomas 15 months after azaserine treatment was 58% in male and 17% in female animals.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Carcinoma incidence 15 months after treatment was 58% in male and 17% in female animals.
raw_record.extra_details: Antimetabolite that induces DNA damage and inhibits DNA synthesis in the rat pancreas. Also induces tumors at kidney, breast, and skin. Given as intraperitoneal injection of 150-260 mg/kg divided into 5-26 weekly doses; atypical acinar cell nodules appear two months after treatment.

raw_record.support_text: Using EPA's linear model for the rate ratio (1 + 0.0068 × cumulative ppm-years), the added cancer risk associated with a continuous environmental exposure to 0.0001 ppm 1,3-butadiene was estimated as 0.88 × 10^-6 for 85 years at risk, with EPA quantifying potential excess leukemia/cancer risks attributable to 1,3-butadiene exposure.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: occupational epidemiological cohort (UAB study, person-years with cumulative ppm-years exposure)
raw_record.extra_details: EPA's Poisson regression model gives rate ratio RR = 1 + 0.0068 × cumulative ppm-years for leukemia; EPA departed from the traditional 70-year default lifetime and assumed an 85-year lifetime, increasing the risk characterization approximately threefold (2.75-fold per Table 1). Choosing the mean dose (370 ppm-years) instead of 250 ppm-years for the highest dose group (>200 ppm-yr) reduces estimated cancer potency by ~22.5% (1.3-fold). Switch to 85-year lifetime increases risk estimate ~3-fold relative to 70 years.

At sacrifice, the cancer control (group 2) group showed cholangiocarcinoma in 15/17 (88.24%) hamsters at week 30 and 11/12 (91.67%) at week 39, whereas the normal, DMN-free control groups showed no cancer, indicating that DMN administration in drinking water induced cholangiocarcinoma in hamsters.

Cholangiocarcinoma graded into five qualitative grades (0 to +4) by percentage of tubular adenocarcinomas.

No p53 loss of heterozygosity in most lymphomas and no point mutations in p53 exons 5-8.

raw_record.support_text: The interpretation states that the risk of squamous cell cancer of the skin is increased by ciclosporin in patients with psoriasis who have been exposed to PUVA. In the nested cohort crossover study (28 ciclosporin users in the PUVA follow-up study), incidence of squamous-cell carcinoma was seven times higher after first ciclosporin use than in the previous 5 years (incidence rate ratio 6·9 [95% CI 4·3–11]), after adjustment for PUVA and methotrexate exposure. Multivariate analysis of the entire PUVA cohort (1380) showed risk of squamous-cell carcinoma after any ciclosporin use close to that for at least 200 PUVA treatments (3·1 [2·6–3·7] vs 2·8 [2·6–3·2]).
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: Psoriasis patients in the PUVA follow-up study cohort (nested cohort of 28 ciclosporin users; entire PUVA study cohort of 1380)
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Increased risk observed in patients with psoriasis who had previously been exposed to PUVA; comparison of frequency of squamous-cell carcinoma before and after first ciclosporin use.
raw_record.extra_details: In the nested cohort, 13 of 28 (46%) developed 169 squamous-cell carcinomas after ciclosporin use (average follow-up 6 years) versus 6 of 28 (21%) with 20 tumours in the 5 years before first use. Risk adjusted for amount of PUVA and methotrexate exposure. Entire-cohort multivariate risk after any ciclosporin use (3·1, 2·6–3·7) was close to that for at least 200 PUVA treatments (2·8, 2·6–3·2). Immunosuppressive treatment associated with increased risk of skin cancer, especially after organ transplant.

raw_record.support_text: The female ACI rat develops mammary cancers when treated continuously with E2 (estradiol), and this propensity behaves as an incompletely dominant trait in reciprocal crosses with the resistant COP strain. Ovariectomy markedly inhibits E2-induced mammary carcinogenesis in the ACI rat, and the tumor-inducing actions of estrogen in the mammary gland are genetically dissociable from those in the pituitary gland.

raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Continuous E2 treatment; ovary-intact, virgin female rats treated beginning at 9 weeks of age.
raw_record.extra_details: Susceptibility to E2-induced mammary carcinogenesis is incompletely dominant and is modified by the Emca1 locus on rat chromosome 5; E2-induced mammary cancers commonly exhibit aneuploidy and widespread allelic imbalance (LOH). E2-induced pituitary growth and hyperprolactinemia were found insufficient for mammary cancer development.

raw_record.support_text: Aflatoxin B₁ was fed at 2 ppm in the diet to pregnant F344 rats from the time of conception and then to their offspring until death. The major causes of death were hepatic neoplasms with metastases; most deaths were from a malignant hemorrhagic liver tumor histologically diagnosed as a hemangiosarcoma, which caused rupture and hemorrhage into the peritoneal cavity or metastases to the lungs. The hemangiosarcomas were readily transplantable and did not produce α-fetoprotein.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Dietary exposure at 2 ppm; pregnant rats exposed from conception through lactation, offspring exposed throughout life (transplacental and milk exposure followed by lifetime dietary exposure).
raw_record.extra_details: Fungal aflatoxins reported to have potent carcinogenic action in rats and other species (refs 1-10). Hemangiosarcomas were transplantable, did not produce α-fetoprotein, and were composed of poorly differentiated endothelial-like cells.

raw_record.support_text: In cohort studies of underground miners occupationally exposed to radon, the relative risk of lung cancer rose linearly with increasing cumulative radon exposure (WLM), both overall and in the region <600 WLM. After allowing a minimum latent period of around five years between exposure and death, the percentage increase in lung cancer risk was higher at about 10 years after exposure than at 20 or 30 years, and greater in individuals aged around 50 than those aged 60 or 70.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: Underground miners in cohort studies (tin, uranium, fluorspar, iron mines; 60,606 exposed miners across eleven studies)
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Occupational exposure in underground mines; risk per unit exposure varied with time since exposure, attained age, and radon concentration/duration.
raw_record.extra_details: Relative risk rose linearly with cumulative exposure; percentage increase per WLM ranged from 0.16 (Yunnan tin mine) to 5.06 (Radium Hill) across studies. Risk per unit exposure was higher in the period ~10 years after exposure than at 20-30 years, and higher at younger attained ages; mines with lower radon concentrations showed a larger percentage increase in risk per unit exposure. raw_record.support_text: In rats that succumb to the mammary carcinogenic effects of PhIP, N-hydroxy-PhIP N3-glucuronide can be detected in urine and breast milk, indicating that N-hydroxylation, the first step in metabolic activation, occurs in vivo in these animals. This passage identifies PhIP as a mammary carcinogen in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: PhIP is a heterocyclic amine (HCA) from cooked meat. Its carcinogenic activity is attributed to metabolic activation to N-hydroxy-PhIP and reactive esters that form guanine adducts; DNA adducts and mutagenesis are considered to play a role in HCA carcinogenesis and in mammary gland cancer initiation. Studies cite a carcinogenic-dose regimen (e.g., 10 doses of PhIP, with ~1% of a 10 mg/kg dose excreted in breast milk) in a rat model (Sprague-Dawley-type lactating rats referenced via Davis et al., Ghoshal and Snyderwine). Related entity N-hydroxy-PhIP (SMILES:8872202) is a metabolite.

raw_record.support_text: Secondary leukemias/myelodysplastic syndromes can occur following treatment with antineoplastic agents. The first type, initially recognized in survivors of Hodgkin's disease, generally presents 5 to 15 years after exposure to alkylating agents such as procarbazine (as part of the MOPP regimen), shares dysplastic features of MDS, and usually progresses rapidly to acute leukemia.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Exposure as part of the MOPP regimen in survivors of Hodgkin's disease; onset generally 5 to 15 years after exposure.
raw_record.extra_details: Alkylating agent. Secondary leukemia shares dysplastic features of MDS, has a high incidence of chromosomal abnormalities involving chromosomes 5 and 7, trilineage dysplasia, significant marrow fibrosis, and usually progresses rapidly to acute leukemia. Presented as treatment-related/secondary MDS.

raw_record.support_text: In this occupational cohort study of benzene-exposed workers, cumulative benzene exposure was modeled against leukemia mortality risk. The linear model showed progressively greater deviance for cumulative exposure as the lag increased from 0-2.5, 5, and 10 years; duration of exposure showed an excess relative risk of 39.2% per year (P=0.004), and average exposure rate showed an excess risk of 7.6% per ppm (P=0.048). The exposure metric best describing the relationship between benzene exposure and leukemia mortality risk was a linear function of cumulative exposure with no lag (excess relative risk 2.3% per ppm-year).
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: occupational cohort of benzene-exposed workers (exposed white males)
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Occupational benzene exposure setting; cumulative exposure without lag was the best-fitting metric.
raw_record.extra_details: Excess relative risk 2.3% per ppm-year (linear, no lag, P<0.001); duration of exposure 39.2% per year; exposure rate 7.6% per ppm; model fit worsened with increasing lag. Cox proportional hazards models. Gender had no significant effect on the exposure-disease relationship.

raw_record.support_text: DMBA treatment induced palpable mammary tumors in rats: in the DMBA control group (Group A), 91.6% of animals had tumors with an average of 8.09 tumors per tumor-bearing rat (tumor multiplicity) at the end of 35 weeks (42 weeks of animal age), with a mean latency period as early as 12 weeks post-carcinogen treatment. Most tumors were between 2 and 5 mm in size, and multiple tumors of different sizes were frequently found. Vanadium and fish oil, given alone or combined, reduced this tumor incidence.
raw_record.extra_details: DMBA was administered as a single injection. Palpable tumors appeared as early as 12 weeks post-carcinogen; 91.6% incidence in DMBA control with multiplicity 8.09 ± 0.68 and tumor volume 1.5 ± 0.03 mm3 in the control (Group A). Vanadium and fish oil were tested as chemopreventive agents and reduced tumor incidence, which is out of scope for carcinogen extraction.

raw_record.support_text: Administration of chlorpromazine to p53 heterozygous and wild-type mice at dose levels up to and including 10 mg/kg did not result in a dose-related increase in tumor incidence or in the type of tumors seen in comparison to controls. Tumor findings were limited: a lymphoma in one p53 heterozygous control female, a prostate sarcoma in one p53 heterozygote, and a single oligodendroglioma in the brain of one 5 mg/kg-dosed p53 heterozygous male; no tumors were observed in control or chlorpromazine-dosed wild-type mice. This is a 26-week carcinogenicity study.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Dose levels up to and including 10 mg/kg; evaluated in a 26-week p53 heterozygous/wild-type mouse study.
raw_record.extra_details: The only tumor seen in chlorpromazine-dosed mice was a single oligodendroglioma in the brain of one 5 mg/kg-dosed p53 heterozygous male, not a dose-related finding. Target tissues were the uterus and ovaries; lower mean uterine weights occurred in p53 wild-type mice at 10 mg/kg with minimal uterine and ovarian atrophy. No chlorpromazine-related histopathologic findings occurred in the p53 heterozygotes.

raw_record.support_text: In a retrospective cohort mortality study of white male cadmium smelter workers, an excess in mortality from lung cancer was observed for the entire cohort (SMR = 149, 95% CI = 95, 222), with greatest mortality among non-Hispanic workers (SMR = 211), among those in the highest cadmium exposure group (SMR = 272), and among workers with 20 or more years since first exposure (SMR = 161). A statistically significant dose-response relationship was evident in nearly all regression models, and the authors performed a quantitative assessment of the risk of lung cancer from exposure to cadmium.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Occupational exposure at a cadmium smelter; workers employed at least 6 months between 1940 and 1969.
raw_record.extra_details: SMR = 149 (95% CI 95, 222) overall; 211 for non-Hispanic workers (95% CI 131, 323); 272 for highest cadmium exposure group (95% CI 123, 513); 161 for 20+ years since first exposure (95% CI 100, 248). Statistically significant dose-response in nearly all Poisson/Cox models. Estimated lifetime excess lung cancer risk at OSHA 100 µg/m3 cadmium fume standard is approximately 50-111 lung cancer deaths per 1000 workers exposed for 45 years.

raw_record.support_text: In NSABP adjuvant breast cancer trials, incidence of treatment-related AML/MDS rose with cyclophosphamide dose intensity: combining regimens E and F (cyclophosphamide 2400 mg/m²/cycle with G-CSF) gave an estimated 5-year cumulative incidence of treatment-related AML/MDS of 1.01% versus 0.21% for standard AC (doxorubicin+cyclophosphamide) regimens, and relative risks versus standard AC ranged up to 6.81 (regimen E, 95% CI 2.84-16.30). The standardized incidence rates indicated AML/MDS was considerably more frequent among treated breast cancer patients than in the general SEER population, consistent with an etiologic, dose-related leukemogenic effect of cyclophosphamide-containing chemotherapy.

raw_record.support_text: Following urethane administration (begun at two or three months of age), 100 per cent of strain-A mice developed pulmonary tumors before they were six months old, with an average of more than 50 tumors per animal. raw_record.support_text: Non-Tg and Tg (human c-Ha-ras transgenic) rats inoculated with DMBA (7,12-dimethylbenz[a]anthracene) developed palpable mammary tumors and adenocarcinomas. Non-Tg rats developed palpable mammary tumors at the highest incidence when inoculated with DMBA at 7 weeks of age, and all Tg rats inoculated with DMBA at 7 weeks of age rapidly developed palpable tumors within 8 weeks, with more than 70% of those initiated at 10, 15 or 20 weeks developing tumors as well. Rats inoculated at 15 and 20 weeks of age showed significantly fewer adenocarcinomas per animal compared with those inoculated at 7 weeks. DMBA is referred to as the chemical carcinogen initiating the tumorigenic response, consistent with the terminal end bud (TEB) being the major target of chemical carcinogens in rat mammary glands.

Cx43-deficient mice showed higher susceptibility to urethane-induced lung adenomas.

raw_record.extra_details: Lung adenomas (solid, papillary, and solid/papillary types) originated from single APTII cells carrying mutations induced by urethane metabolites; CYP2E1 is the main enzyme responsible for urethane metabolism in lung; mouse strain influences susceptibility (strain A most susceptible, C57BL less, Swiss/CD1 intermediate).

raw_record.support_text: Etoposide, which is being increasingly used in ALL, induces chromosomal changes in the 11q region, leading rapidly (within about 2 years) to a secondary acute myelomonocytic/monoblastic leukaemia with 11q23 rearrangements. The risk for this complication may be increased by the simultaneous use of other topoisomerase II inhibitors and L-asparaginase, and was as high as 6% in recent pediatric series. The paper also notes, in the secondary-tumours section, that several active anti-ALL drugs, including etoposide, bear the risk of second cancers.

raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Therapy-related secondary leukaemia; risk may be increased by simultaneous use of other topoisomerase II inhibitors and L-asparaginase; exact incidence in adult ALL survivors not known.
raw_record.extra_details: Leukaemia develops within about 2 years; induced via chromosomal changes in the 11q region; incidence was as high as 6% in recent pediatric series. Etoposide also listed among anti-ALL drugs bearing the risk of second cancers.

NTP classified these chemicals in male rats as showing 'clear or some evidence of carcinogenic activity.'

All 17 hamsters developed papillomatous tumors including pre-cancerous or cancerous lesions; additional topical DMBA application induced neoplastic transformation forming carcinoma in situ or early invasive SCC, and invasive SCC was produced by the 10th week. Acetone-only treated pouches showed only epithelial hyperplasia with chronic inflammation.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Repeated topical application (three times/week, 0.5% DMBA in acetone) to the hamster buccal pouch, continued until the 13th week.
raw_record.extra_details: DMBA exposure sequentially produced hyperorthokeratosis, squamous papilloma with or without mild epithelial dysplasia, carcinoma in situ, early invasive SCC (EISCC), and finally well-differentiated/invasive SCC by week 10. This was a chemoprevention study in which hamsters were also fed diets containing 150, 500, or 1500 ppm celecoxib (COX-2 inhibitor) as a potential chemopreventive agent; celecoxib is not extracted as a carcinogen.

raw_record.support_text: The epidemiology data on ethylene oxide (EO) exposure were assessed for leukemia response using cumulative external concentration (ppm-years) as the dose measure in the combined UCC/NIOSH worker cohort. Response data were assessed in terms of relative risk (rate ratio), and a relative risk measure that assumes a multiplicative relationship between EO exposure and the background rate of leukemia was applied to characterize the dose–response relationship within the range of observation, treating the EO–leukemia association as evidence of carcinogenic risk in humans.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: UCC/NIOSH combined cohort of ethylene oxide workers
raw_record.extra_details: Dose-response modeled using cumulative external EO concentration grouped into four dose groups (0-33, 33-125, 125-285, >285 ppm-years) with person-year weighted averages (7.4, 64.8, 187.4, 477.7 ppm-years); relative risk/rate ratio assessed; Poisson regression adjusted for age, sex, and calendar year; background hazard from UCC workers unexposed to EO; a multiplicative relationship between EO exposure and leukemia background rate was assumed; point-of-departure ED10-LED10 to ED000001 considered consistent with USEPA guidelines; risk estimates were relative risk converted to added/extra risk.

raw_record.extra_details: Described as a potent carcinogen found in tobacco (18-50 ng per cigarette); a significant pro-carcinogenic substance requiring metabolic activation. raw_record.support_text: A single intragastric administration of DMBA (7,12-dimethylbenz[a]anthracene) has been shown to induce mammary tumors in young, cycling female Sprague–Dawley rats. The carcinogen interacts with rapidly proliferating cells in the terminal end buds, forming DNA adducts that participate in transforming normal terminal end bud cells to malignant pathways. Susceptibility to DMBA is maximal at 55 to 60 days of age and is abolished by ovariectomy, suggesting the carcinogen's action depends on ovarian secretions.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Induction in young, cycling female Sprague-Dawley rats; susceptibility maximal at 55-60 days of age; effect abolished by ovariectomy, indicating dependence on ovarian secretions; single intragastric dose.
raw_record.extra_details: DMBA referred to as a 'carcinogen'; mechanism involves DMBA-DNA adduct formation in terminal end bud cells; estrogenic properties allow interaction with estrogen receptor and partial mimicry of estradiol feedback in ovariectomized rats. The study uses DMBA as an initiator to test the potency of melatonin (10 mg/kg) in limiting cancer initiation versus tumor progression.

The paper describes this as the experimental induction of buccal pouch carcinomas by DMBA.

raw_record.extra_details: Also abbreviated as DMBA. Tumors showed squamous-cell-carcinoma features including pleomorphism, hyperchromatism, keratin pearls, and hyper-proliferation; cavitary tumors extended over the mucosal surface and onto facial skin. DMBA treatment also increased OPN mRNA expression in buccal mucosa with exposure time; transformed squamous cells expressed OPN at markedly increased levels.

raw_record.support_text: In a re-analysis of the UAB synthetic rubber worker cohort, the maximum likelihood estimate of the coefficient of cumulative butadiene (BD) ppm-years in a linear rate ratio model for deaths in which leukemia was the primary or a contributing cause of death was 0.00153 (SE 0.00083, 95% CI -0.0001 to 0.0032), with a likelihood-ratio test p-value of 0.004 and a Wald test p-value of 0.033, statistically significant at the 5%/1% levels. The coefficient increased at lower cumulative exposure cutoffs (e.g., 0.00466 at ≤500 ppm-years, p=0.003 by likelihood ratio test), indicating an exposure-response relationship between cumulative BD exposure and leukemia death. Corresponding leukemia SMRs were elevated (e.g., 124 for all person-years) and leukemia death rate ratios rose with increasing cumulative BD ppm-years categories (e.g., rate ratio 3.31 for the 829.8+ ppm-years category). The analysis also found the cumulative number of BD peaks (exposures above 100 ppm) was the exposure covariate most correlated with and predictive of the observed leukemia.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Occupational exposure in UAB synthetic rubber worker cohort; leukemia defined as primary or contributing cause of death; exposure-response shown by statistical association rather than an explicitly causal designation; peak exposures above 100 ppm (BD peaks) were the exposure covariate most strongly correlated with leukemia.
raw_record.extra_details: Linear rate ratio coefficient per cumulative BD ppm-year was 0.00153 (SE 0.00083) for all data with likelihood-ratio p=0.004 and Wald p=0.033; coefficients rose at lower cumulative exposure cutoffs (0.00466 at ≤500 ppm-years, LR p=0.003; 0.00303 at ≤1000 ppm-years). Leukemia SMR (primary cause) was 124 for all person-years; mortality rate ratios per cumulative exposure category reached 3.31 for the 829.8+ ppm-years category. USEPA risk-assessment slope of 0.0099 ppm-year was referenced. Analyses adjusted for age, years since hire, calendar year, and race. BD metabolism and genotoxicity (gene mutations, chromosomal aberrations) discussed as mode of action supportive of frequent exposures exceeding saturation/tolerance thresholds.

raw_record.support_text: The early stages of the carcinogenic process induced by aflatoxin B₁ (AFB₁) in rat liver during 24 weeks of feeding and the resulting tumours were studied with respect to cytokeratin (CK) expression. Tumours maintained CK patterns in normal (BL8L) and hepatoma (JB1) cell lines.

raw_record.support_text: Azoxymethane (AOM) is described as one of the most widely used colon-specific carcinogens. AOM-induced tumors contain genetic mutations affecting signaling pathways relevant to human disease and progress through pathologic stages from aberrant crypt foci (ACF) to invasive cancer. The DNA adducts formed in rodents by this carcinogen are also found in human colonic tissues, suggesting a comparable environmental stimulus for neoplasia. In the same study, azoxymethane is referred to as a colorectal carcinogen used for chemical induction of colonic tumorigenesis in mice.
raw_record.extra_details: Widely used colon-specific carcinogen; AOM-induced tumors carry mutations in signaling pathways relevant to human disease and progress from aberrant crypt foci to invasive cancer. Azoxymethane (AOM) and its precursor-related DNA adducts form in rodents and are also found in human colonic tissues (suggested comparable environmental stimulus for neoplasia). Used for chemical induction of colorectal carcinogenesis in mice in this study.

The investigators believe the emerging excess is real, but continued follow-up will help confirm it.

raw_record.extra_details: Dose-response analysis of Pliofilm data with life-table analysis of concentration; peak exposure concentrations argued more critical than ppm-years; benzene-induced leukemia thought to involve multiple clastogenic benzene metabolites whose delivered doses below the DNA-repair threshold confer no leukemogenic risk; benzene metabolized by hepatic CYP2E1 to phenolic and ring-opened products, with metabolites responsible for bone marrow toxicity rather than the parent compound.

raw_record.extra_details: MNU referred to as a 'carcinogen'; all 32 rats developed mammary neoplasms (31/32 carcinomas, one lactating adenoma); tumour incidence ~5 tumours per rat; most carcinomas were invasive (87%) and locally aggressive, with ulceration of skin in 6/32; metastases to spleen, liver and lymph node observed in 2/32 (6%) rats 14 weeks after first MNU application; model proposed for studying malignant progression of mammary tumours.

raw_record.support_text: In the pathology analysis, in both BALB/cAnNCrl and C57BL/6J strains, ENU-treated males had a very high incidence of malignant T-lymphoblastic lymphoma. The case for lymphoma being induced by ENU is described as clear-cut because the very high incidence (>75% of those culled sick) at a relatively young age is considerably greater than the background incidence (9-34%) in untreated BALB/cAnNCrl and C57BL/6J mice, and a survey of 28 retired untreated C57BL/6J breeding males found no thymic lymphomas.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Claim applies to male mice in a breeding/mutagenesis programme; incidence >75% of those culled sick at relatively young age compared with 9-34% background incidence.
raw_record.extra_details: Alias: ENU. Incidence greatly exceeds background (9-34%) in untreated mice on two-year ageing studies; survey of 28 retired untreated C57BL/6J male breeders found no morbidity between 6-12 months and no thymic lymphomas. Associated with strain-specific susceptibility and putative perturbation of DNA repair and tumour suppressor pathways. ENU also described as a stem-cell mutagen causing immunosuppression.

raw_record.support_text: Streptozotocin, known to induce diabetes through islet cell damage, was studied in the BOP-treated hamster model. Administration of streptozotocin alone caused islet cell tumors (44%), pseudoductules (40%), and ductular adenomas (12%), and the authors conclude that streptozotocin has tumorigenic activity at relatively low dose; simultaneous treatment with streptozotocin and BOP produced a significantly higher incidence of ductular carcinomas than BOP alone.
raw_record.extra_details: Tumorigenic at relatively low dose; also caused pseudoductules (40%) and ductular adenomas (12%) alone. Combined with BOP it enhanced ductular carcinoma incidence; pretreatment at a diabetogenic dose (50 mg/kg, three i.p. injections) prevented BOP-induced pancreatic cancer, and this inhibition could be blocked with nicotinamide. i.v. dosing (30 mg/kg) used in the combined-treatment arm.

raw_record.support_text: WT, Xpa and Xpa/p53 mice were fed CsA (cyclosporine) in their diet for 39 weeks to study carcinogenic features of the compound. CsA treatment resulted in a higher incidence of lymphomas in Xpa/p53 mice compared with untreated mice or exposed WT mice. The CsA-induced lymphomas were of a pleomorphic type resembling follicular center cell lymphoma, and no differences in CsA-induced tumor types were observed between the three genotypes. Other tumor types found in CsA-treated mice (bronchioloalveolar adenoma, osteosarcoma, hemangiosarcoma of spleen and liver, adenocarcinoma or adenomatous polyp in small intestine) occurred sporadically, were equally distributed across genotypes, and were judged probably not treatment related.

raw_record.support_text: The incidence of hepatocellular adenomas and/or carcinomas was significantly increased in male rats given 900 and 1800 ppm Metofluthrin and in female rats given 1800 ppm Metofluthrin. The parameters related to the key events in Metofluthrin-induced liver tumors were observed at or below the tumorigenic dose levels in males and females.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Increased incidence in male rats at 900 and 1800 ppm and in female rats at 1800 ppm given in feed.
raw_record.extra_details: Induction was accompanied by species- and tissue-specific key events (increased liver weight, hepatocellular hypertrophy, increased smooth endoplasmic reticulum, increased BrdU-labeling index, altered hepatic foci), all showing parallels in dose response and strong temporal association with the tumor response; tumor increase was slight relative to current and historical controls. Metofluthrin is a pyrethroid.

condition_group: route=oral+species=rat

raw_record.support_text: In the two-year rat carcinogenicity bioassay, metofluthrin increased hepatocellular adenoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, and combined adenoma+carcinoma incidences at 900 and 1800 ppm in both sexes. In males the combined adenoma+carcinoma counts were 8 (p<0.05) at 900 ppm and 12 (p<0.01) at 1800 ppm; in females the combined count was 12 (p<0.01) at 1800 ppm, versus a control of 1.
raw_record.extra_details: Doses 200, 900, and 1800 ppm administered in diet; significant combined adenoma+carcinoma increases at 900 and 1800 ppm. The MOA was attributed to phenobarbital-like CYP2B enzyme induction with consequent increased cell proliferation, and the tumorigenic effect was described as weak even at doses near (900 ppm) or in excess (1800 ppm) of the MTD.

raw_record.support_text: Administration of medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA) to BALB/c female mice induced mammary ductal carcinomas with a mean latency of 52 weeks and an incidence of about 80%. raw_record.extra_details: Induced tumors were hormone-dependent (HD), metastatic, and expressed both estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR).

raw_record.support_text: Using a protocol in which MPA was given as a s.c. 40 mg silastic pellet replaced by a 20 mg pellet 6 months later, MPA proved to be carcinogenic in female BALB/c mice, with a mammary carcinoma incidence of 58%. raw_record.extra_details: Incidence 58%; 89% ductal and 11% lobular carcinomas; ductal hyperplasias or carcinoma in situ in most animals without frank carcinoma; occasional lymph node and lung metastases and tumor cells in veins; ductal tumors expressed high ER, PR and prolactin receptors.

raw_record.support_text: Diethylnitrosamine (DENA) is described as a powerful chemical carcinogen frequently used to induce animal models of liver malignancies. In the liver it is metabolized into reactive electrophilic reactants that alter DNA and form alkyl DNA adducts, leading to chromosomal aberrations, micronuclei, and sister chromatid exchanges in hepatocytes, with the eventual end-stage lesions being mainly multifocal hepatocellular carcinomas (HCCs) superimposed on varying degrees of liver cirrhosis.
raw_record.extra_details: Also spelled diethylnitrosamin (DENA). Metabolized in the liver into reactive electrophilic reactants that form alkyl DNA adducts, causing chromosomal aberrations, micronuclei, and sister chromatid exchanges. Multifocal HCCs arise superimposed on liver cirrhosis. Reported administration regimes include addition to drinking water (usually 100 ppm), transoral intragastric delivery, and intraperitoneal injection, with 3-6 months needed for HCC formation.

raw_record.support_text: In the skin, Cav-1 (−/−) mice demonstrate hypersensitivity to carcinogen-induced epidermal tumors. Following 16 weeks of treatment with the carcinogen DMBA (7,12-dimethylbenz[a]anthracene), Cav-1 (−/−) null mice show very significant increases in tumor incidence, tumor area, and tumor number per mouse compared with wild-type counterparts. The carcinogen DMBA thereby induces epidermal (skin) tumors in this intact-mouse model.
raw_record.extra_details: Referred to by the alias DMBA. Treatment lasted 16 weeks; Cav-1 null mice showed very significant increases in tumor incidence, tumor area, and tumor number per mouse compared with wild-type controls, reflecting hypersensitivity to the carcinogen.

raw_record.support_text: The attributable fraction of lung cancer caused by radon was calculated as the ratio of lifetime lung cancer death risk caused by radon relative to all-cause mortality. An estimated 11.15%–77.42% of lung cancer deaths among non-smokers, 11.02%–72.55% among smokers, and 10.78%–77.33% among ex-smokers in the Stei area over 13 years was attributed to radon exposure, and analogous figures were computed for Torrelodones. The radiation risk could be about 1.6–1.7 times higher in smokers due to radon–smoking interaction.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: residents of the Ștei area (Romania) and Torrelodones (Spain)
raw_record.extra_details: Annual lung cancer deaths attributable to indoor radon estimated at 132 (95% CI 120–144) to 291 (95% CI 248–302) depending on model (Darby, Lubin, BEIR VI). Mean radon exposures in Stei ranged 57–1550 Bq m-3. Estimated with BEIR VI exposure age-duration model. Risk ~1.6–1.7x higher in smokers (radon–smoking interaction). No other cancers showed significantly higher mortality.

raw_record.extra_details: DEN (alias: DEN) administered by feeding over 8 weeks for long-term exposure, with experiment terminated at the 16th week; DEN-induced HCC used as a standard experimental model of hepatocarcinogenesis and for screening anti-HCC compounds. raw_record.support_text: In the ED01 (mega-mouse) study, the carcinogenicity of 2-acetylaminofluorene (AAF) was tested in BALB/c mice by chronic feeding, and it produced bladder and liver tumors. For bladder tumors the average latency period at 150 ppm in the feed was 19.8 months; the bladder dose-response showed a different NOEL and a steeper slope than for liver. The authors concluded that the bladder neoplasm data do not contradict the 'no-threshold' theory of carcinogenesis.

raw_record.support_text: In a rat carcinogenicity bioassay with quinacrine dosed intrauterine on study days 0 and 21, the only neoplasms related to quinacrine administration were in the reproductive tract (uterus, cervix, and vagina). The overall incidence of these 'uncommon tumors' (all tumors excluding benign endometrial stromal polyps) rose with dose: 0.7% in controls, 2% at 10/10, 6.8% at 70/70, 13% at 70/250 and 15% at 70/350 mg/kg, versus a 2% historical control rate.

raw_record.support_text: In this series, patients with solid tumors developed keratoacanthoma-type squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) shortly after starting sorafenib therapy. Six patients who continued taking sorafenib continued to develop SCCs, whereas patients switched to sunitinib and patients who discontinued sorafenib stopped developing new SCCs during follow-up (6 weeks to 14 months). The oldest patient (#15) developed 15 SCCs, the greatest number in the study, during a period of increased sorafenib dosing (to 600 mg/d).
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: patients taking sorafenib for solid tumors
raw_record.extra_details: Clinical case series; SCCs arose within weeks of sorafenib initiation; continued sorafenib was associated with continued SCC development, while switching to sunitinib (no Raf signaling inhibition) or discontinuing sorafenib resulted in no new SCCs. One patient developing 15 SCCs had a prior history of basal cell carcinoma. Associated hypertrophic actinic keratoses showed evidence of micro-invasive SCC in some cases.

raw_record.support_text: Syrian golden hamsters underwent choledochojejunostomy and then received subcutaneous injections of the chemical carcinogen N-nitrosobis(2-oxopropyl)amine every 2 weeks at a dose of 10 mg/kg body wt, starting 4 weeks after surgery and continuing for 18 weeks. Intrahepatic biliary adenomas developed in all control animals (15/15), and intrahepatic biliary carcinomas were present in 13 (87%) hamsters in the control group. The results indicate that ONO-1714 represses N-nitrosobis(2-oxopropyl)amine-induced biliary carcinogenesis in bilioenterostomized hamsters.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Subcutaneous injections every 2 weeks at 10 mg/kg body wt, starting 4 weeks after choledochojejunostomy and continuing for 18 weeks; animals killed 22 weeks after surgery.
raw_record.extra_details: The agent is explicitly referred to in the paper as 'the chemical carcinogen'. In the ONO-1714-treated group the incidence of intrahepatic biliary adenomas (7/15, 47%) and carcinomas (6/15, 40%) was significantly reduced versus control, demonstrating a chemopreventive effect of NO suppression, but the carcinogenicity of N-nitrosobis(2-oxopropyl)amine itself is the basis of the model.

raw_record.support_text: For benzene, the US EPA unit risk estimate is based on the Pliofilm cohort, studied repeatedly by different researchers, and the exposure-response relationships are based on no more than 15 deaths from leukemia among workers mainly exposed to benzene levels above 20 ppm. The authors question extrapolating human cancer risk at low levels from occupational studies with high-level exposure, since protein adduct formation per unit exposure is higher at low exposure. Studies in Australian, Swedish, and Norwegian oil refinery workers reported substantially increased or two-fold risks of leukemia at benzene exposures that were lower than in the Pliofilm cohort.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: oil refinery workers (Pliofilm cohort and Australian, Swedish, Norwegian refinery cohorts)
raw_record.extra_details: US EPA unit risk estimate based on the Pliofilm cohort; exposure-response based on about 15 leukemia deaths; most workers exposed above 20 ppm (60 mg/m3). Low-level exposure produced ~10-fold higher protein adducts per ppm of reactive metabolites (benzene oxide, 1,4-benzoquinone) than 50-100 ppm due to CYP2E1 saturation; authors caution against extrapolating low-level risk from high-level occupational studies.

raw_record.support_text: Estragole (1-allyl-4-methoxybenzene) has been well studied over the past 30 years and is a rodent hepatocarcinogen in bioassays. The evidence for its carcinogenic activity derives from at least eight chronic murine cancer bioassays involving different periods of exposure, routes of administration, and species. Its carcinogenic activity is related to phase I and II metabolism, with 1'-hydroxyestragole and a 1'-sulfate ester carbocation acting as the proximate and ultimate carcinogen, respectively, forming DNA adducts implicated in induction of liver tumors.
raw_record.extra_details: Carcinogenic activity derives from at least eight chronic murine bioassays with varying exposure periods and routes. Mechanism: CYP450-mediated 1'-hydroxylation (CYP1A2, CYP2A6 most important; CYP2D6, CYP2C19, CYP2E1 lesser), followed by sulfation forming an unstable carbocation that binds DNA; main stable guanine adduct (E-3'-N2-dGuo) implicated in liver tumor induction. raw_record.support_text: The finally selected continuous ERR model for the German uranium miner Wismut cohort is linear in radon exposure with exponential effect modifiers depending on age at median exposure, time since median exposure, and radon exposure rate; the central estimate of ERR/WLM for lung cancer is 0.0054 (95% CI: 0.0040; 0.0068) at mean age at median exposure of 30 years, mean time since median exposure of 20 years, and an exposure rate of 3 WL. The ERR was estimated to decrease with increasing age at median exposure, with time since median exposure, and with increasing exposure rate, and the model's indication of a non-linear radon exposure response was not supported by a non-significant quadratic term (P = 0.28). Abnormal foci, nodules and adenomas are detected by ~6 months, and hepatocellular carcinomas (HCCs) appear at ~10 months.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Single injection into 15-day-old male mice at 1.25-5 µg/g body weight, a time when hepatocytes are still proliferative; nontoxic doses
raw_record.extra_details: Commonly abbreviated DEN; earlier foci, nodules and adenomas appear by ~6 months and HCCs by ~10 months; early focal lesions show decreased cytoplasmic ATPase and glucose-6-phosphatase and increased glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, indicating a metabolic shift from gluconeogenesis to glycolysis with increased cell proliferation (refs 22-25).

raw_record.support_text: DEN-induced hepatocarcinogenesis is strongly supported by the finding that the incidence and multiplicity of liver tumor induced by DEN are significantly reduced in Cyp2e1-null mice; the paper refers to DEN-induced HCC and DEN's carcinogenic metabolites produced via Cyp enzymes. The authors report that DEN chronically administered for up to 18 weeks promotes hepatocarcinogenesis and provide a mouse model that resembles human HCC.
raw_record.extra_details: DEN (N-nitrosodiethylamine) at doses of 2.5, 5, and 20 mg/kg given chronically for up to 18 weeks induces HCC in young-adult mice; associated with decreased Cyp2e1 protein/activity, increased ROS and 4-HNE levels, cell proliferation, inflammation and fibrosis. A single-DEN-injection model is also referenced. Cyp2e1-null mice show reduced DEN-induced tumor incidence/multiplicity but not complete prevention, implicating additional Cyps (e.g., Cyp2a6) in DEN metabolic activation.

raw_record.support_text: In the in vivo mouse model, mice began to form hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) 7-10 months after injection of DEN (N-nitrosodiethylamine) solvent, establishing DEN-induced HCC. Alcohol and the drug teniposide were then administered at 6 months of age under DEN stress, and tumour number analysis and H&E staining of liver sections showed that teniposide reduced tumour numbers, whereas the Alcohol+NC group had the most obvious liver lesions.
raw_record.extra_details: DEN is referred to as 'DEN solvent' used to establish the HCC model; tumours formed 7-10 months after injection. The paper's main focus is the therapeutic effect of teniposide on alcohol-associated HCC (A-HCC), with DEN used as the tumor-inducing agent.

Findings initially involved exposures above the levels permitted in industrial countries (in the range of 1-40 ppm) and were later seen even at exposures around one part per million, the then-current U.S. standard, in Chinese shoemakers with certain common genetic traits who showed loss of bone marrow function and lowered white blood counts.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: factory/shoemaker workers in twelve cities in China
raw_record.extra_details: Cancer of the bone marrow was described as clearly worsened with greater benzene exposures, initially at exposures of roughly 1-40 ppm and more recently at around 1 ppm. At 1 ppm, Chinese shoemakers with certain common genetic traits showed loss of bone marrow function and lowered white blood cell counts, a condition noted as capable of leading to anemia and leukemia.

raw_record.support_text: The study used two genotoxic carcinogens, X-rays and ENU, to probe the mechanism of carcinogenesis. ENU dissolved at pH 6.0 in reverse-osmosis-purified water; administered in brown bottles because of instability, with mice consuming ~3 ml/day. Direct comparative carcinogenesis experiment evaluating dose-dependent and combined effects with X-rays.

raw_record.support_text: Among 4775 exposed watch dial painters, 35 cancers of the paranasal sinuses and the mastoid air cells were reported, a rate of 0.7%, compared with an extremely low background rate. These head cancers are described as radium-induced (see p.136).
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: cancers of the paranasal sinuses and the mastoid air cells
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Occupational exposure from watch dial painting
raw_record.extra_details: 35 cancers among 4775 exposed painters (0.7% incidence). Background paranasal sinus cancer ~0.03% of reported cancers. Tumor-type distribution in radium-exposed head cancers: 56% epidermoid (cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma), 34% mucoepidermoid, 10% adenocarcinoma; mucoepidermoid cancers of these cavities described as a signature for high-level radium exposure. Latency: first bone tumor at 5 years, first paranasal sinus/mastoid cancer at 19 years, most head cancers >30 years after exposure (BEIR IV).

condition_group: model=radium-exposed persons+species=human

raw_record.support_text: Cancers of the paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells have a longer latency period after exposure to radium than do bone cancers: the first bone tumor was diagnosed 5 years after exposure, whereas the first cancer of the paranasal sinuses or mastoid air cells was observed 19 years after exposure.
raw_record.extra_details: Bone tumors referred to as arising after radium exposure with about half arising within 30 years; latency comparison presented relative to paranasal sinus/mastoid cancers.

raw_record.support_text: Mice exposed to benzo[a]pyrene (BaP) at a low dose in combination with a sub-carcinogenic dose of arsenic showed formation of lung adenoma, with the carcinogenic effect enhanced several fold. CYP1A1 converts BaP to BaP-7,8-oxide, forming bulky DNA adducts, and arsenic potentiates the binding of BaP to cellular DNA as much as 18-fold in vivo, leading to oxidative DNA damage and eventually tumorigenesis.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Lung adenoma formation in this study was observed at a low BaP dose combined with arsenic co-exposure (enhanced several fold).
raw_record.extra_details: BaP (abbreviation). Metabolic activation via CYP1A1 to BaP-7,8-oxide and further to the bay-region diol epoxide forming bulky DNA adducts.

raw_record.support_text: Administration of DMBA to virgin mice of both BALB/c and BALB/cfC3H strains resulted in a moderate frequency of mammary tumors within 40 wk after treatment. DMBA-induced tumor incidences were 6% and 7% at 18 wk and 29% and 36% at 38 wk after treatment of BALB/c and BALB/cfC3H mice, respectively. The paper describes DMBA as the chemical agent used in murine mammary tumorigenesis and refers to the tumors as chemical carcinogen-induced tumors.

raw_record.extra_details: Moderate tumor frequency within 40 wk; incidences 6% and 7% at 18 wk and 29% and 36% at 38 wk for BALB/c and BALB/cfC3H, respectively. Described as chemical carcinogen in murine mammary tumorigenesis.

raw_record.extra_details: Reported t-MDS/AML rates of 3% at 5 years, 10% at 8 years, and up to 25% at 10 years; t-MDS/AML had a grim prognosis with median survival under 3 months; also used at high dose in HDT/SCT where MDS/AML cases were seen; mechanism includes direct DNA damage.

raw_record.support_text: OSHA estimated that a working lifetime of 45 years of exposure to benzene at 10 ppm would cause an excess leukemia risk of 95 leukemia deaths per 1,000 exposed workers, deaths that are above background and attributable to benzene exposure. The new standard was projected to prevent at least 326 deaths from leukemia and diseases of the blood and blood-forming organs among US workers, and OSHA's earlier proposal stated that the risks of leukemia and other benzene-related health effects needed to be reduced by a reduced permissible exposure limit.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: US workers occupationally exposed to benzene
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Occupational exposure; quantitative estimate based on 10 ppm 8-hour TWA over a 45-year working lifetime.
raw_record.extra_details: OSHA estimated 95 excess leukemia deaths per 1,000 workers over a 45-year working lifetime at 10 ppm exposure, with a minimum 90 percent reduction in excess risk under the 1 ppm standard and at least 326 prevented leukemia/death-of-blood-diseases cases. Standard lowered 8-hour TWA from 10 ppm to 1 ppm and STEL from 25 ppm to 5 ppm (52 FR 34460, September 11, 1987).

raw_record.extra_details: Also known as BBN. Given at 0.05% concentration in drinking water; induces bladder tumors in 95% of rodents after 25 weeks. The oncofetal genes H19 and IGF2 are abundantly expressed in BBN-induced bladder cancer after 11 weeks of carcinogen administration. The authors report not using the BBN-induced model because of the long time needed for tumor production (25 weeks) and risk of exposure to carcinogenic material.

raw_record.support_text: The NTP 2-year bioassay (NTP, 2008b) reported a statistically significant increase in the incidence of adenomas in the duodenum of female mice at ≥172 mg/l SDD relative to concurrent controls. Combined intestinal tumor incidence (adenomas plus carcinomas) was significantly elevated at ≥172 mg/l SDD, pointing to Cr(VI) as the cause of small intestinal tumorigenesis in mice.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: female mice (similar results in male mice, NTP 2-year bioassay)
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Exposure via drinking water as sodium dichromate dihydrate (SDD); significant for duodenal adenoma at ≥172 mg/l SDD.
raw_record.extra_details: Carcinogenic effect attributed to Cr(VI); proposed mode of action is cytotoxic and nonmutagenic, involving villous cytotoxicity, sustained compensatory crypt hyperplasia and crypt cell mutagenesis leading to tumorigenesis. Tumors confined to the portal of entry (small intestine), absent in rats. First intestinal neoplasm observed at day 451, consistent with late tumor onset.

raw_record.support_text: The present DMBA-induced mammary carcinogenesis study in +/fa and +/+ rats with and without 10% corn oil diet showed that +/fa rats proved more susceptible to DMBA-induced mammary carcinogenesis than +/+ controls, and this might be partly related to higher early-stage serum leptin levels. Corn oil diet possibly contributed to the growth of mammary tumors via elevated serum leptin levels, and an aggressive carcinoma phenotype with activated MAPK cascade (nor estrogen signaling) was found predominantly in +/fa rats.
raw_record.extra_details: DMBA was used to induce mammary carcinogenesis; +/fa rats were more susceptible than +/+ controls, partly attributed to higher early-stage serum leptin levels. raw_record.support_text: Urethane exposure induced tumorigenesis in mouse lungs: no tumors were observed in the control group, tumors started appearing at 12 weeks after urethane injection, and well defined lung adenomas were observed at 36 weeks after urethane exposure, with tumor area ranging between 0.0315 and 4.581 mm² (average 0.629 mm²). This urethane-induced lung tumorigenesis was inhibited by oral administration of IP6 (phytic acid), which prevented tumor development by about 53% at 36 weeks.
raw_record.extra_details: Urethane (ethanediamine). Tumors appeared starting at 12 weeks and were clearly visible at 36 weeks after first injection; hyperplasia observed at 4 weeks. Used as the tumor-inducing agent in a study of the chemopreventive effect of IP6 (phytic acid), which inhibited urethane-induced tumorigenesis by ~53% at 36 weeks and ~65% at 12 weeks. IP6 alone produced no tumors in drinking water.

Respiratory tract cancers were significantly increased (16 v 9; SMR = 1.76, CI = 1.03-2.9), but this did not attain significance when only subjects with ≥5 years exposure and ≥10 years latency were considered, and there were no dose-response relations with cumulated toluene dose (ppm-years). No significant increases occurred at other sites, including leukaemias/lymphomas/myelomas.
raw_record.extra_details: No overall excess tumours (SMR 1.26, CI 0.95-1.7); respiratory tract cancers increased (SMR 1.76, CI 1.03-2.9) but non-significant after ≥5 yr exposure and ≥10 yr latency and with no dose-response by cumulated ppm-years; no excess leukaemias/lymphomas/myelomas. Exposure to benzene had occurred up to the early 1960s. Air toluene peaked ~450 ppm in the 1940s-50s and ~30 ppm by mid-1980s.

raw_record.support_text: In a population-based case-control study across eight Canadian provinces (2,390 lung cancer cases, 3,507 controls), the authors conclude these findings provide further evidence that radon is an important risk factor for lung cancer and that risks are unevenly distributed across Canada. In multivariate models, a 50 Bq/m³ increase in average health-region radon was associated with a 7% (95% CI: -6-21%) increase in the odds of lung cancer, and for every 10 years individuals lived in high geological-based radon areas the odds of lung cancer increased by 11% (95% CI: 1-23%).
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: Canadian adults in a population-based case-control study across eight provinces
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Residential/ecological exposure in high-radon geographic areas of Canada
raw_record.extra_details: Residential radon exposure history over 20 years used with two mapping methods (Health Canada survey of ~14,000 residential radon measurements aggregated to health regions; geological radon risk areas from geology, sediment geochemistry, aerial gamma-ray spectrometry). Health-region average radon ranged 16-386 Bq/m³; high geological radon areas ranged 0-100%. Odds of lung cancer rose 7% (95% CI -6-21%) per 50 Bq/m³ and 11% (95% CI 1-23%) per 10 years in high-radon areas. Hierarchical logistic regression adjusted for individual and geographic covariates.

raw_record.support_text: In a 2-year NTP carcinogenicity bioassay, male F344/N rats exposed to tert-butyl alcohol (TBA) in drinking water at 1.25, 2.5, and 5.0 mg/ml showed increased incidences of renal (kidney) tubular adenomas and carcinomas. In step sections, adenomas + carcinomas were significantly increased at the 2.5 mg/ml dose (18 cases vs 7 controls) together with multiple adenomas (9 vs 1), and combined standard and step sections showed a statistically significant increase in adenomas + carcinomas at 2.5 mg/ml (19 vs 8). The passage notes 'No other tumor types were increased in either rats or mice.'
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Drinking water exposure for 2 years; statistically significant increases in renal adenomas+carcinomas and multiple adenomas were primarily noted at the 2.5 mg/ml (mid) dose.
raw_record.extra_details: 2-year NTP bioassay (modified from NTP, 1995). Linear papillary mineralization and renal hyperplasia also increased with dose. Significant decreases were seen in Harderian gland adenomas+carcinomas and pancreatic islet cell adenomas/carcinomas in affected male dose groups and in mammary adenomas/fibromas/carcinomas and mononuclear leukemia in female rats.

raw_record.support_text: Carcinogenicity study results with phenolphthalein in 1997 triggered greater interest in the P53+/- assay. The p53-deficient (+/-) mouse model responded to phenolphthalein treatment with a carcinogenic response of thymic lymphomas after only 4 months of dosing, and phenolphthalein had previously resulted in thymic lymphomas in male and female B6C3F1 mice in 2-year studies (NTP 1996). These findings resulted in removal of phenolphthalein from the over-the-counter (OTC) market in 1999.

raw_record.support_text: The study investigated azoxymethane (AOM)-induced colon carcinogenesis in male albino Swiss mice, which received intraperitoneal injections of AOM (10 mg/kg) once a week for two consecutive weeks. AOM-induced mice exhibited alterations in the histological structure of the colon, elevated lipid peroxidation and nitric oxide, declined glutathione content, and reduced activity of superoxide dismutase and glutathione peroxidase. The study indicated clearly that the number of liver neoplasms induced by the treatment was simply proportional to the dose rate and that even quite low dose rates caused a variety of non-neoplastic liver abnormalities such as hyperplastic nodules.

raw_record.support_text: The application of DEN (diethylnitrosamine) to mice induces liver damage, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The developing liver tumours can be visualized by enzyme and immunohistochemical stainings and by magnetic resonance imaging; a moderate-to-severe animal burden results from the intraperitoneal administration protocol using a single DEN dose of 10-25 mg/kg at 14 days of age or 50-90 mg/kg at 5-6 weeks.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Intraperitoneal injection in male mice; hepatocarcinogenesis is influenced by sex and age; doses of 10-25 mg/kg (14-day-old mice) or 50-90 mg/kg (5-6 week old mice).
raw_record.extra_details: DEN (diethylnitrosamine) also induces liver damage, fibrosis, and cirrhosis; tumour development is dose- and time-dependent; associated with elevated serum transaminases, collagen/fibrotic marker expression, and variable alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) expression, though AFP was not a reliable predictor of hepatocarcinogenesis; moderate-to-severe severity classification.

raw_record.support_text: The paper states that DEN (diethylnitrosamine) is a representative chemical carcinogen whose mechanism of action involves forming ethyl adducts at N- and O-atoms in DNA bases. DEN treatment for 12-16 weeks in a rat model progressively produced preneoplastic GGT-positive lesions and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
raw_record.extra_details: Alias DEN / diethylnitrosamine. Described as a representative chemical carcinogen; mechanism involves ethyl adduct formation at N- and O-atoms of DNA bases. Produced preneoplastic GGT-positive lesions (preneoplastic and tumor lesions) and increased Gstp1 mRNA during HCC development.

condition_text: Early-life limited-duration exposure (10 weeks starting at 4 weeks of age) in a stop-exposure design, evaluated at 98 weeks; findings apply in the absence of phenobarbital, which did not enhance or inhibit DCA effects.

raw_record.support_text: In the absence of phenobarbital, early-life exposure to dichloroacetic acid (DCA) increased the incidence and number of hepatocellular tumors in male and female B6C3F1 mice compared with controls in a stop-exposure/promotion study (10 weeks of DCA at 1.0, 2.0, or 3.5 g/l in drinking water starting at 4 weeks of age, assessed at 98 weeks). Significant dose trends were observed in both sexes, and at the high dose, 10 weeks of prior DCA treatment induced comparable effects (≥85% tumor incidence and number) to continuous lifetime exposure. The authors concluded that early-life exposure to DCA may be as carcinogenic as life-long exposures.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Early-life limited-duration exposure (10 weeks starting at 4 weeks of age) in a stop-exposure design, evaluated at 98 weeks; findings apply in the absence of phenobarbital, which did not enhance or inhibit DCA effects.
raw_record.extra_details: DCA is a structural analog of pyruvate; inhibits PDH kinase and is characterized as a metabolic programming agent; proposed mechanism is epigenetic-mediated effects related to cellular metabolism. Significant dose trends in both sexes; high-dose effects comparable to continuous lifetime exposure (≥85% tumor incidence). Doses used: 1.0, 2.0, 3.5 g/l. Prior DCA treatment did not cause persistent liver cytotoxicity or preneoplastic changes and did not alter DNA sequence variant profiles in liver tumors. Tumors include hepatocellular adenoma (HA) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HC). Also noted that DCA has been studied experimentally as a cancer therapy.

raw_record.support_text: NTP concluded there was clear evidence of carcinogenicity in male rats based on the increased incidence of kidney tumors at 750 ppm of ethylbenzene inhaled for lifetime. raw_record.support_text: In the Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group comparisons of 5 years of endocrine therapy, there were fewer uterine cancers and more bone fractures with aromatase inhibitors than with tamoxifen. Aggregating the five comparisons, the 10-year incidence of endometrial cancer (defined as any uterine cancer except cervix cancer) was 0.4% in the aromatase inhibitor group versus 1.2% in the tamoxifen group (absolute difference 0.8%, 95% CI 0.6–1.0; p<0.0001), with the proportional increase with tamoxifen roughly independent of age and persisting for some years after treatment ended; the absolute excess with tamoxifen was 0.7% at ages 55–69 and 1.4% at older ages.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: women with early breast cancer in randomized trials comparing five years of tamoxifen versus aromatase inhibitor endocrine therapy
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: endometrial cancer (uterine cancer excluding cervix cancer)
raw_record.extra_details: Excess endometrial cancer with tamoxifen was relative to aromatase inhibitor treatment (RR for the decrease with aromatase inhibitors 0.33, 95% CI 0.21–0.51): 10-year incidence 1.2% with tamoxifen vs 0.4% with aromatase inhibitors (absolute difference 0.8%, 0.6–1.0; p<0.0001), including five versus nine deaths. Increase was approximately independent of age, persisted for some years after treatment ended, and the absolute excess with tamoxifen was 0.7% (0.5–0.9) at ages 55–69 and 1.4% (0.5–2.4) at older ages. There was no significant effect on any other cancer type except contralateral breast cancer.

The paper uses DMH as an experimental colon carcinogen induced in Wistar rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Carcinogenic via its metabolite azoxymethane and ultimate carcinogenic metabolite methyldiazonium ion which methylates DNA in colonic epithelial cells. raw_record.support_text: Prospective cohort studies in humans evaluated the relationship of AFB1 exposure with HCC incidence. In a nested case–control study in a Shanghai cohort of 18,244 men, presence of AFB1 biomarkers (metabolites and AFB1-N7-guanine adducts) was associated with liver cancer (RR 3.8; 95% CI 1.2–12.2 after adjusting for HBsAg), and a follow-up found that any urinary AFB1 biomarker significantly predicted liver cancer (RR 5.0; 95% CI 2.1–11.8). In the Taiwan Cancer Screen Project, detectable AFB1-albumin adducts gave a 5.5-fold increased HCC risk on Penghu, and across the full cohort AFB1-albumin adducts (RR 1.5, 95% CI 1.0–2.6) and AFB1 metabolites (RR 1.8, 95% CI 1.2–2.6) were associated with HCC.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: Humans, specifically cohort participants in Shanghai (PR China) and rural townships of Taiwan with hyperendemic HBV infection
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Risk applies to dietary ingestion of AFB1-contaminated foods; studied in HBV-hyperendemic populations with interaction between AFB1 and HBV infection.
raw_record.extra_details: Prospective evidence: Shanghai nested case–control within 18,244 men (22 cases), RR 3.8 (95% CI 1.2–12.2) for AFB1 metabolites/AFB1-N7-guanine; strong AFB1-HBV interaction (RR 60.1; 95% CI 6.4–561, only 7 cases/2 controls positive for both); follow-up with 50 cases RR 5.0 (95% CI 2.1–11.8) for any urinary AFB1 biomarker. Taiwan CSP (12,024 men, 13,594 women): 5.5-fold HCC increase with AFB1-albumin adducts (Penghu); AFB1-albumin RR 1.5 (95% CI 1.0–2.6), urinary AFB1 metabolites RR 1.8 (95% CI 1.2–2.6); fourfold HCC risk in HBsAg-negative individuals with urinary AFB1 metabolites >=77 fmol/ml. Ecological and case–control biomarker data were discordant, with only AFB1-DNA adducts in leukocytes significantly associated with risk in case–control studies.

raw_record.support_text: BD rat strains exhibit phenotypic differences regarding ethylnitrosourea (ENU)-induced carcinogenesis in the peripheral nervous system. Premalignant Schwann cells carrying a point mutation in the Neu/Erbb2 gene diagnostic for the resulting MPNST emerge shortly after ENU exposure in both strains, but mutant cells expand in trigeminal nerves of BDIX rats until full-blown tumors are present, whereas they disappear in BDIV nerve tissue about 3 months after neonatal ENU exposure.

raw_record.extra_details: ENU-induced MPNST is characterized in premalignant Schwann cells by a Neu/Erbb2 point mutation diagnostic for the resulting MPNST; mutant cells disappear from BDIV nerve tissue about 3 months after neonatal ENU exposure.

raw_record.support_text: Spironolactone has been shown to be a tumorigen in chronic toxicity studies in rats. In one study using 25, 75 and 250 times the usual daily human dose (2 mg/kg) there was a statistically significant dose-related increase in benign adenomas of the thyroid and testes. In female rats there was a statistically significant increase in malignant mammary tumors at the mid-dose only. In male rats there was a dose-related increase in proliferative changes in the liver, and at the highest dosage (500 mg/kg) effects included hepatocytomegaly, hyperplastic nodules and hepatocellular carcinoma, the last not statistically significant.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: benign adenomas of the thyroid and testes
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Statistically significant dose-related increase at 25, 75 and 250 times the usual daily human dose (2 mg/kg) in chronic toxicity studies.
raw_record.extra_details: Spironolactone described as a tumorigen in chronic toxicity studies in rats. In male rats a dose-related increase in proliferative changes in the liver was noted; at the highest dosage (500 mg/kg) effects included hepatocytomegaly, hyperplastic nodules and hepatocellular carcinoma, the last not statistically significant.

The discussion concludes in paragraph 52 that the weight of epidemiological evidence suggests hydralazine is not carcinogenic in man.

raw_record.support_text: Oral administration of benzo(a)pyrene (B(a)P, 50 mg/kg body weight) to Swiss albino mice induced lung carcinogenesis, raising lipid peroxides and lung tumor markers such as carcinoembryonic antigen and neuron specific enolase, while decreasing enzymatic and non-enzymatic antioxidants. The study used this B(a)P treatment as a lung carcinogenesis model, and luteolin was administered to assess its chemopreventive potential against this induced lung carcinogenesis.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Administered at 50 mg/kg body weight by oral (p.o.) administration.
raw_record.extra_details: Induced raised lipid peroxides (LPO) and lung tumor markers CEA and NSE, with decreased antioxidants (SOD, CAT, GR, GPx, GST, GSH, vitamin E, vitamin C); associated with upregulated PCNA, CYP1A1 and NF-kB expression. Also known by aliases B(a)P and benzo (a)pyrene. Luteolin (15 mg/kg p.o.) was evaluated for chemopreventive activity against this induced carcinogenesis.

raw_record.extra_details: Crude OR 1.38 (95% CI 1.116–1.706); adjusted OR 1.246 (95% CI 1.004–1.547); each 100 mg increase adjusted OR 1.029 (95% CI 1.005–1.054). Risk presented as evidence of the carcinogenic effects of AA on renal tissue.

raw_record.support_text: MNNG (N-methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine) was found to be a very potent gastric carcinogen in Mongolian gerbils; treatment with 400 ppm of MNNG in drinking water for 50 weeks resulted in 64% gastric adenocarcinomas in the gerbils. Administration of MNNG in the drinking water of rats over their life span resulted in adenomatous tumors only in the glandular epithelium of the stomach. The mouse glandular stomach was relatively resistant to MNNG.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: 400 ppm MNNG in drinking water for 50 weeks; mouse glandular stomach relatively resistant to MNNG
raw_record.extra_details: Aliases: MNNG, N-methyl-N'-nitroguanidine. Under acidic conditions MNNG is converted to N-methyl-N'-nitroguanidine, which alkylates purine bases of DNA, RNA, and some amino acids leading to mutations. In rats, lifetime drinking-water administration produced adenomatous tumors only in the glandular epithelium of the stomach.

raw_record.support_text: Radon exposure in homes is described as producing radon-induced lung cancer deaths. Reductions in lung cancer deaths are projected from lowering indoor radon levels, and the analysis references the EPA central estimate of risk, corresponding to about 4,000 lung cancer deaths averted annually, with each pCi/L reduction in a residence equating to roughly 0.01 lung cancer deaths averted over a 50-year period.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Indoor residential exposure; risk estimates based on the EPA central estimate of risk.
raw_record.extra_details: Radon is a radioactive noble gas. Analyses address remediation of homes exceeding 4 pCi/L; projecting radon-induced lung cancer death reductions (about 22% under Distribution II) and about 4,000 lung cancer deaths averted annually, and roughly 0.01 lung cancer deaths averted per pCi/L reduction in a single residence over 50 years.

raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Rutile-type pigment-grade TiO₂ at 250 mg/m³ (MTD) for 2 years producing particle overload; benign bronchoalveolar adenomas significantly increased and the keratinizing response may reflect a normal biological response to particle overload in rat lungs.
raw_record.extra_details: Whole-body exposure 6 h/d, 5 d/week at 10, 50 or 250 mg/m³; tumors only at 250 mg/m³; survival comparable to controls. raw_record.support_text: The relative risk of developing lung cancer from cumulative exposure to radon (occupational plus natural) is modeled using the BEIR VI model, which assumes radon exposure has a multiplicative effect on the baseline rate of lung cancer. The RR represents the ratio of the probability of developing lung cancer among occupationally exposed people to that among non-occupationally exposed people, and it decreases with increasing time since exposure and increases with attained age. The model is applied to employees up to 64 years old.

raw_record.extra_details: Model by the Biological Effects of Ionizing Radiation (BEIR) VI Committee. Exposure expressed in work level months (1 WLM = 170 h × 20.8 µJ/m³ = 3.54 mJ×h/m³). Beta slope = 0.0768; exposure-age-concentration model with time windows 5-14, 15-24, ≥25 years prior to attained age; age modification factors θ<55=1, 55-64=0.57, 65-74=0.29, ≥75=0.09; λz=1. Model intentionally not adjusted for smoking.

raw_record.support_text: Prenatal exposure of rats on day 13 of gestation to ENU (N-ethyl-N-nitrosourea) induced forebrain gliomas. In animals receiving ENU alone, forebrain glioma frequency was 26.8% in brains with no or minor dysplasia and 69.4% in brains with major dysplasia. The tumors were located in the subependymal/periventricular layer and cortical white matter, and this diaplacental neurocarcinogenesis was described as enhanced with increasing degree of brain dysplasia.

raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Transplacental administration on day 13 of gestation; glioma frequency associated with the degree of simultaneously induced brain dysplasia (highest in major-dysplastic brains).
raw_record.extra_details: ENU abbreviation; known as diaplacental neurocarcinogenesis. Glioma frequency ENU alone: 26.8% (no/minor dysplasia) vs 69.4% (major dysplasia). In the combination arm ENU was given at 50 mg/kg with X-irradiation (0.5-1.5 Gy). Tumor multiplicity and preferential periventricular location increased with dysplasia.

The fundic mucosa also showed marked atypical hyperplasia with changes in foveolar cells similar to those seen in early incomplete metaplasia. The paper notes a previous study in rats also showed late development of carcinoid tumours of the fundus after prolonged loxtidine administration.

Vinyl chloride-reported as mutagenic (chromosomal aberrations, micronucleus, sister chromatid exchange, Ki-ras and p53 mutations), mechanistically linked to increased HCC risk.
