raw_record.support_text: In rats, sustained chronic daily oral (dietary) benfluralin exposure at high dose levels produced thyroid follicular cell hyperplasia (KE4) and, as the adverse outcome, increased thyroid tumors consisting of follicular cell adenomas and carcinomas, which began appearing at 1 year and increased after 2 years. The tumors were observed together with the key-event profile of liver CAR/PXR activation, liver UGT induction, decreased circulating T4 and increased TSH, occurred above a threshold of about 100 mg/kg/d, and were regarded as secondary to the liver effects. The overall assessment concluded the proposed MOA is highly consistent in rats but lacks relevance to humans owing to differences in thyroid physiology and sensitivity, with no convincing evidence that this liver-enzyme-induction mechanism carries an increased human thyroid cancer risk.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: thyroid follicular cell adenomas and carcinomas
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Sustained, chronic high-dose dietary exposure only (above a threshold of about 100 mg/kg/d); threshold- and time-dependent; thyroid effects secondary to liver enzyme induction; the MOA is rat-specific and considered not relevant to humans.
raw_record.extra_details: Non-genotoxic agent, negative for mutagenic, clastogenic and DNA-altering potential; no thyroid peroxidase or sodium-iodide symporter inhibition; no direct thyroid cytotoxic effect; MOA parallels phenobarbital and other liver enzyme inducers; negative in amphibian metamorphosis assay ('probably thyroid inactive').

raw_record.support_text: BHA (butylated hydroxyanisole) caused carcinomas in the rat forestomach when fed at high dietary concentration for prolonged periods. Although humans have no anatomically equivalent region to the rat forestomach and human exposure levels are more than a thousand-fold lower, there is continued concern over whether BHA could be a human carcinogen. The hyperplasia preceding tumour development, which showed a dose-dependent cell-damage response, was noted as critical to this discussion.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: High dietary concentration fed for prolonged periods; humans lack an anatomically equivalent forestomach region and human exposure levels are >1000-fold lower.
raw_record.extra_details: Continued concern over whether BHA could be a human carcinogen despite the species/route differences. Tumor development preceded by hyperplasia; the hyperplasia is interpreted as a response to dose-dependent cell damage, with non cell-damaging doses unlikely to induce hyperplasia or neoplasia. Related observations: BHA inhibits prostaglandin synthesis and 2% BHA caused focal necrosis/ulceration of the forestomach after 1 week and marked hyperplasia/parakeratosis after 3 weeks; 5-HT hypersecretion implicated in adaptation to high levels of the antioxidant.

raw_record.support_text: To assess tumor initiation in a carcinogen-driven early lung cancer model, 6- to 8-week-old C57BL/6 mice (homozygous LRRK2 knockout or wild type strain mates) received 10 weekly intraperitoneal injections of urethane (ethyl carbamate, 1 g/kg diluted in PBS) and were sacrificed at 26 weeks post-first injection. WT mice produced an average of 2.53 ± 0.91 visible lung adenomas per animal (n = 16) while LRRK2 KO mice produced 6.53 ± 0.75 adenomas per animal (n = 20), and KO adenomas were larger on average (0.78 ± 0.02 mm vs 0.53 ± 0.06 mm in WT). The title explicitly identifies urethane as a carcinogen present in cigarette smoke, and the text describes this as carcinogen-driven early lung cancer.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: C57BL/6 mouse (wild type and LRRK2 knockout)
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Administered as 10 weekly intraperitoneal injections of 1 g/kg in PBS; animals sacrificed at 26 weeks post-first injection; LRRK2 knockout increased adenoma multiplicity and size compared to wild type.
raw_record.extra_details: Also referred to as urethane; described as a carcinogen present in cigarette smoke. WT mice averaged 2.53 ± 0.91 adenomas/animal (n=16, 95% CI 0.702–4.36) vs 6.53 ± 0.75 in LRRK2 KO (n=20, Welch's t-test P=0.0020). No sex-specific differences were found; Ki-67 positivity was equivalent between genotypes.

A quantitative cohort of 58,677 German uranium miners (1946-2003) confirmed an association between silica exposure and lung cancer, particularly for high exposures (exposure limit >10 mg/m³). raw_record.support_text: The study established a chemically induced rat mammary tumor model using N-methyl-N-nitrosourea (MNU), which has long been used in preclinical breast cancer research. An intraductal (i.duc) injection of MNU (1 mg per duct, 20 µL) into the fourth mammary gland of pubescent female Sprague-Dawley rats induced atypical hyperplasia at 4 weeks that progressed to stable carcinoma in situ at 5–6 weeks, with tumors located predictably in the mammary gland. The conventional approach using intraperitoneal or intravenous carcinogen injection induces tumors at unpredictable locations.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: carcinoma in situ of the mammary gland (atypical hyperplasia progressing to carcinoma in situ)
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Intraductal administration (20 µL, 1 mg per duct) into the fourth mammary gland; carcinoma in situ developed 5–6 weeks after treatment.
raw_record.extra_details: Described as a potent carcinogenic agent and the longest-known of the nitroso compounds, causing DNA alkylation without requiring metabolic activation. Tumors expressed ER positively, Her-2 negatively, and low Ki-67. Model produced predictable tumor location and better consistency than conventional i.p/i.v injection.

raw_record.extra_details: Cumulative exposure was the strongest predictor among cumulative exposure, duration of exposure, and average exposure rate; interaction and quadratic terms did not improve fit. raw_record.support_text: Benzene is described as a leukemogenic chemical associated with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). According to Khalade et al., benzene exposure increased AML risk in a dose-response pattern: low exposure (<40 ppm-years) increased risk by a factor of 1.64, medium exposure (40–99.9 ppm-years) by 1.90, and high exposure (>100 ppm-years) by 2.62. It is hypothesized that benzene accelerates hematological malignancies by altering lymphocyte function and destabilizing stromal and endothelial cells in the stem cell (HSC) niche. The section is headed 'Benzene and other known occupational exposures.'
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Presented in the context of occupational exposure to benzene.
raw_record.extra_details: Dose-response relative risks for AML: 1.64 for low exposure (<40 ppm-years), 1.90 for medium exposure (40–99.9 ppm-years), 2.62 for high exposure (>100 ppm-years), per Khalade et al. Mechanism hypothesized to involve altered lymphocyte function and destabilized stromal/endothelial cells in the HSC niche.

This is the inducer/positive-control model; dietary kawain (a kavalactone) demonstrated anti-initiation and anti-promotion effects against OH-BBN-induced urothelial tumorigenesis, reducing bladder tumor burden and invasive carcinoma incidence.

raw_record.support_text: The text describes AOM (azoxymethane) treatment inducing colorectal carcinoma (CRC) tumors and carcinogenesis in murine animal models. Mice of different genetic backgrounds show distinct sensitivity (A/J and SRJ/R highly sensitive, C57B/L6 and Balb/c moderately sensitive), with tumor crypts composed of closely packed cells and neoplastic cells infiltrating the muscular wall of the distal colon; no metastases or invasion were observed even in the high-sensitivity strain. The model is suitable for early-stage but not late-stage or metastatic CRC.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Mouse strain governs sensitivity (A/J and SRJ/R highly sensitive; C57B/L6 and Balb/c moderately sensitive); model suited to early-stage, not late-stage or metastatic CRC; in described protocols AOM is given by intraperitoneal injection and may be combined with DSS (AOM/DSS colitis-associated CRC model) or TNBS.
raw_record.extra_details: AOM abbreviation; used widely to evaluate chemopreventive/therapeutic strategies and mechanistic insights into human CRC risk factors; no metastasis or invasion observed; DSS added to drinking water at 2-10% in the AOM/DSS model; TNBS co-administration (10 mg/kg AOM i.p. plus 2.5 mg TNBS i.r. in 50% EtOH) produced inflammatory, dysplasia, or carcinoma lesions.

raw_record.support_text: The study assessed the impact of the Propionibacterium freudenreichii (PF) probiotic against colorectal cancer (CRC) induced by azoxymethane (AOM) in SD rats. Methylene blue staining of colon tissues showed that PF administration significantly reduced the formation of colonic aberrant crypt foci (ACF) compared to the AOM control group, and the results reveal that consuming PF inhibits the carcinogenic effects of AOM. Thus AOM is used as the inducing carcinogen that produces CRC and colonic ACF in the rats.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: colorectal cancer / colonic aberrant crypt foci
raw_record.extra_details: AOM was used to induce CRC in SD rats (four groups: normal control, AOM group, PF 1 x 10^9 CFU/mL, and 5-fluorouracil 35 mg/kg standard drug control). PF supplementation reduced ACF formation and suppressed lipid peroxidation (lower colon malondialdehyde) relative to the AOM control, and PF inhibited the carcinogenic effects of AOM.

raw_record.support_text: Radon, an inert gas produced by the natural decay of uranium, has been considered the main risk factor for lung cancer after cigarette smoke and is classified as a group one carcinogen by the IARC. Different studies found a linear correlation between LC risk and Radon exposure, and a multicenter case-control study in Galicia and Asturias found a higher LC risk at residential Radon levels above 200 Bq·m-3 (OR 2.33, 95% CI 1.40-3.89), with an interaction with tobacco smoking (OR 2.75).
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Radon indoor levels above 200 Bq·m-3
raw_record.extra_details: Inert gas from the natural decay of uranium; main LC risk factor after cigarette smoke; alpha particles from decay products (e.g., Polonium-218) linked to a carcinogenic effect via DNA base mutations and chromosomal strand breaks; interaction with tobacco smoking exposure (OR 2.75, 95% CI 1.44-5.25); trend similar in women and those spending more than 20 years in the same residence.

raw_record.support_text: The investigators challenged lean and obese B6 mice with the chemical carcinogen 3′-methylcholanthrene (MCA) and tracked tumor incidence for four months. MCA induces de novo sarcomas over a longer time course, allowing the immune system to interact with a developing tumor from the earliest stages of oncogenesis: 47% of lean B6 mice remained tumor-free by 120 days while only 16% of obese B6 mice were tumor-free.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Administered as a single subcutaneous injection of 50 μg; sarcoma development monitored out to 120 days.
raw_record.extra_details: Explicitly labeled the 'chemical carcinogen' MCA; induces de novo sarcomas over a longer time course so the immune system interacts with a developing tumor from early oncogenesis. Tumor-free at 120 days: 47% of lean B6 vs 16% of obese B6 mice; tumor incidence in obese B6 mice was similar to Rag2−/− mice lacking adaptive immunity.

raw_record.support_text: In a leukemia risk assessment among benzene-exposed workers, the excess risk of leukemia increased with increasing cumulative air benzene exposure (Ptrend = 0.0001). The excess leukemia risks for workers exposed to <3, 3–5, 5–12, and ≥12 mg/m3·year were 4.34, 4.37, 4.44, and 5.52 × 10−4, respectively, all exceeding the EPA's lower bound acceptable carcinogenic risk value of 1 × 10−6. The discussion notes that a case-cohort study also revealed a dose-dependent association between cumulative benzene exposures and acute myeloid leukemia, and each of the four exposure groups exceeded the EPA's lowest acceptable limit for carcinogenic risk.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Risk estimated from linearized multistage (LMS) modeling; excess leukemia risk noted as a potential risk of developing leukemia among the 5 workers with air benzene below the limit of detection (leukemia risk 4.32 × 10−4).
raw_record.extra_details: Excess leukemia risks estimated from S-PMA and t,t-MA (urinary benzene metabolites used as internal dose) were slightly higher than from air benzene concentrations; t,t-MA-derived risk was closest to air-benzene-derived risk. LMS model parameters derived from leukemia incidence data in a Chinese benzene cohort. EPA and Singapore semi-quantitative models also applied; Singapore and LMS models gave consistent high-risk findings.

The degree of lesion development was in direct proportion to duration of treatment, with malignant lesions appearing in one animal only 5 months after DES implantation and extensive lesions after 11-14 months. It was concluded that DES is carcinogenic in the squirrel monkey, although the mechanism of carcinogenicity could not be proven to be due to its estrogenic activity.

raw_record.extra_details: Three remaining animals manifested extra-genital serosal lesions involving the adrenal glands, spleen, and mesentery. Mechanism of DES carcinogenicity could not be proven to be due to its estrogenic activity.

raw_record.support_text: TOTH and SHIMIZU: A 0.01% solution of methylhydrazine was administered daily in the drinking water of 6-week-old randomly bred Syrian golden hamsters for the remainder of their lifetime. The treatment gave rise to malignant histiocytomas of liver and tumors of the cecum. Malignant histiocytomas developed in 32% of the females and 54% of the males whereas among the controls no such lesions were seen; tumors of the cecum occurred in 18% of females and 14% of males versus 1% in controls.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Administered daily as a 0.01% solution in drinking water from 6 weeks of age for lifetime.
raw_record.extra_details: Incidence: 32% of females and 54% of males; no such lesions in controls. Methylhydrazine is a rocket fuel component.

raw_record.support_text: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a significant contributor to a subset of HCC cases and is described as a potent carcinogen that promotes HCC by forming DNA adducts through its reactive intermediate, AFB1-8,9-epoxide (AFBO), which induces genetic alterations in liver cells, most notably mutations in the p53 gene. HCC is particularly prevalent in regions with high AFB1 exposure levels.
raw_record.extra_details: Potent carcinogen; promotes HCC via AFBO DNA adduct formation and p53 gene mutations. In a study of HCC samples from individuals with significant AFB1 exposure in Guangxi, China, CTNNB1 mutations were found in 5/62 cases (~8%) but 20/41 showed positive β-catenin staining, suggesting possible Wnt pathway activation.

raw_record.support_text: Diethylstilbestrol (DES), a synthetic estrogen prescribed to women between 1940 and 1971 to prevent miscarriage and premature labor, was reported from the late 1990s to increase cancer risk in women exposed to DES in utero. In the largest cohort of 4,536 DES-exposed and 1,544 unexposed daughters, three cases of vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma occurred among the exposed daughters, yielding a standardized incidence ratio of 40.7 (95% CI, 13.1–126.2) compared with the population. This was sufficient to warrant a ban on the use of the drug during pregnancy.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: cohort of 4,536 DES-exposed and 1,544 unexposed daughters
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: In utero exposure during pregnancy
raw_record.extra_details: Synthetic estrogen used 1940-1971 to prevent miscarriage and premature labor; 3 cases among exposed daughters, SIR 40.7 (95% CI 13.1-126.2); finding sufficient to warrant a ban on use during pregnancy. Also reported increased risk of high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (preinvasive lesion, excluded) in up to 4% of exposed women.

raw_record.support_text: The study investigated whether dietary selenium can reduce respiratory tract tumours induced by the indirect-acting carcinogen benzo[a]pyrene (BaP). In the experimental protocol, Syrian golden hamsters were instilled intratracheally with 8 mg BaP + 8 mg ferric oxide suspended in saline, once every 2 weeks for 16 weeks, and the respiratory tract tumours induced were examined at terminal autopsy.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Administered as 8 mg BaP + 8 mg ferric oxide suspended in saline; intratracheal instillation once every 2 weeks for 16 weeks; co-administered with ferric oxide carrier.
raw_record.extra_details: BaP is described as an indirect-acting carcinogen. The study examines whether dietary selenium, in low-fat (normal) and high-fat diets, can reduce BaP-induced respiratory tract tumours. Respiratory tract tumours were classified according to the Becci classification, adapted. The IARC method used for tumour statistical analysis is a statistical method, not an IARC carcinogenicity classification.

raw_record.extra_details: F-diAA was administered in the diet; carcinogen-containing diet given for 4 weeks followed by 1 week on basal diet until total 16 weeks of F-diAA administration, then basal diet for the remaining 28 weeks before animals were killed. Results were scored by a method accounting for hyperplastic lesions, number/size of neoplasms, presence of metastases, and time to lesion development; animals dying before 26 weeks were excluded because 26 weeks is required to develop a small carcinoma of the liver.

raw_record.extra_details: Grown/observed across multiple time points (65, 95, and 120 weeks). In males a similar proportion of hepatoma-bearing mice was seen at 65, 95, and 120 weeks after 30 weeks of treatment, whereas in females incidence increased from week 65 to 95; hepatomas larger than 10 mm were more frequent at 95 and 120 weeks. Storage levels of DDT and metabolites measured in liver and interscapular fat; levels fell after treatment stopped but remained above untreated controls even after 90 weeks.

condition_text: Direct intrapulmonary implantation in a beeswax/tricaprylin pellet vehicle; dose-dependent induction, with squamous metaplasia preceding carcinoma development.

raw_record.support_text: In female Osborne-Mendel rats, graded doses (0.005–0.5 mg) of 3-methylcholanthrene (MCA) added to 0.05-ml beeswax/tricaprylin pellets and injected directly into the lower peripheral left lung produced a progressive series of epithelial lesions at the pellet surface: keratinizing squamous metaplasia, keratinizing squamous dysplasia, overt squamous cell carcinoma, and undifferentiated neoplasms. The squamous cell carcinomas developed from the pool of metaplastic lesions at rates and frequencies directly related to dose. The beeswax/tricaprylin vehicle alone produced only a bland granulomatous infiltrate, indicating the vehicle was noncarcinogenic.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: squamous cell carcinoma of the lung (epidermoid carcinoma)
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Direct intrapulmonary implantation in a beeswax/tricaprylin pellet vehicle; dose-dependent induction, with squamous metaplasia preceding carcinoma development.
raw_record.extra_details: Doses tested: 0, 0.005, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50 mg MCA. Metaplastic lesions appeared by 17 weeks; carcinoma developed from the metaplastic pool at rates directly related to dose, but not proportional to the frequency of initial metaplasia (low doses gave lower metaplasia:carcinoma ratios). Vehicle (beeswax/tricaprylin) alone produced only bland granulomatous infiltrate. Undifferentiated neoplasms also observed. Present study described as an advantageous model for screening potential pulmonary carcinogens.

raw_record.support_text: Groups of 20 male Wistar rats were fed diets containing 0 (control), 0.2, 1.0, and 5.0% Ponceau MX for 15 months. The most pronounced pathological finding was the development of hepatic cell adenomas in rats that had ingested the dye for more than 10 months, indicating a liver tumorigenic effect of Ponceau MX. Growth was retarded at the 1 and 5% levels, and liver-to-body weight ratio was increased at all levels.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Adenomas developed in rats that ingested the dye-containing diet for more than 10 months during a 15-month feeding study; dietary levels were 0.2, 1.0, and 5.0%.
raw_record.extra_details: Azo dye. Hepatic cell adenomas were the most pronounced pathological finding. Renal lesions (marked tubular degeneration, some glomerular changes) were observed in both treated and control groups and were not dose-attributable tumors; growth retardation at 1 and 5%, increased water consumption, increased liver/body and kidney/body weight ratios were also reported. ³⁵S-labelled Ponceau MX absorption studies localized significant radioactivity only in liver and kidney.

raw_record.support_text: 4-Ethylsulphonylnaphthalene-1-sulphonamide (HPA) was shown to be carcinogenic to the bladder epithelium of the C57 × IF mouse. Long-term oral administration/feeding induced papillomas and carcinomas of the bladder epithelium; female mice (44 per cent carcinomas) were more susceptible than males (16 per cent), with male (21 per cent) and female (28 per cent) castrates intermediate.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: C57 × IF mouse; Ab × IF F1 hybrid mouse
raw_record.extra_details: Alias HPA; originally synthesized as an anticonvulsant and diuretic. Long-term feeding to Ab × IF F1 mice gave papillomas and carcinomas of the bladder epithelium, significantly more frequent in females. Female C57 × IF mice (44% carcinomas) more susceptible than males (16%), castrates intermediate. Species susceptibility varies: induced epithelial hyperplasia in rat and in certain mouse types, but the dog and guinea pig were resistant and the rabbit was apparently not susceptible; hamster developed epithelial hyperplasia less readily than the mouse. The hyperplasia induced after 2 or 6 weeks administration correlated with the ultimate tumour incidence.

raw_record.support_text: The present studies injected 50-day-old Buf/N female rats with a single dose of NMU (N-nitroso-N-methylurea; 30 µg per g body weight) to ensure tumour induction from a single carcinogenic insult. Under these conditions, latency periods ranged from 6 to 12 months and resulted in the almost exclusive induction of mammary carcinomas in the injected rats.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Single dose of 30 µg per g body weight injected into 50-day-old Buf/N female rats; latency period 6-12 months.
raw_record.extra_details: NMU induced mammary carcinomas in 90% of animals with a latent period of about 60 days per prior studies by Gullino and co-workers (paragraph p:4); tumours were essentially exclusively mammary carcinomas. Carcinogenic effect appears hormonally regulated: castration before NMU injection decreases tumour incidence to negligible levels, whereas ovariectomy after NMU treatment leaves tumour frequency unchanged but reduces number of carcinomas per animal and increases latency.

raw_record.support_text: A NIOSH-reported cohort of 748 white male rubber workers employed during 1940-49 who died between 1950 and 1975 had 7 deaths due to leukemia versus 1.38 to 1.48 expected, a highly statistically significant excess. The implication drawn is that benzene levels below those capable of causing overt pancytopenia can cause leukemia, supporting a no-threshold linear dose-response between benzene and acute myelogenous leukemia.

raw_record.qualifying_conditions: The paper's author argues this study does not allow conclusions about leukemia risk from benzene below the current standard because AML occurred at <1% incidence and there were opportunities for very high exposures; average exposure was ≤10 ppm but some exposures reportedly exceeded 300 ppm.
raw_record.extra_details: 7 leukemia deaths vs 1.38-1.48 expected, statistically significant. Findings were a centerpiece in OSHA's move to lower the benzene standard from 10 ppm to 1 ppm. Supports a no-threshold linear dose-response idea for benzene and acute myelogenous leukemia.

Estimated lifetime incidence of excess leukemia of 1.4% to 15.2% for workers exposed to current allowable levels. raw_record.support_text: In experiment 1, a male rat given a single intragastric dose of NMU developed an odontogenic tumour at 8 months, arising as a pale warty mass from the gingival margin distal to the lower right incisor which was interpreted clinically as carcinoma. Histologically the lesion was a gingival papilla expanded by a plexiform arrangement of odontogenic epithelium set in mesenchyme resembling the basal pulp organ, with predentine and mineralized tubular dentine, enamel matrix, and keratin-containing cells resembling the ghost-cells of the calcifying odontogenic cyst. Sections of the adjacent incisor were normal. A comparable odontogenic tumour at the angle of the mandible (dysplastic dentine, cementum and enamel with odontogenic epithelium) was also seen in a rat in experiment 2.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: odontogenic tumour (gingival, interpreted clinically as carcinoma)
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Single dose; male rat; intragastric administration.
raw_record.extra_details: Abbreviation NMU. In experiment 2 a second odontogenic lesion was found at the angle of the mandible as a complex mass of dysplastic dentine, cementum and enamel surrounded by odontogenic epithelium with ghost-cell keratinization. The gingival tumour showed foreign-body giant-cell reaction to escaped keratin. No naming/unapproved identifiers used for the mandibular lesion.

raw_record.support_text: In a randomized trial of patients with polycythemia vera, treatment with chlorambucil was associated with a statistically significant excess incidence of leukemia compared with patients treated with 32P or phlebotomy (|t| = 2.04 in the Cox model, 0.01<P<0.025). The average excess incidence of leukemia in chlorambucil-treated patients was 3.5 times that in the other two groups combined (approximate 95% CI, 1.6 to 7.6). raw_record.extra_details: Chlorambucil is compared with 32P and phlebotomy treatment groups. Twelve of 16 chlorambucil leukemia cases occurred after three years; incidence of leukemia in the chlorambucil group was 10 of 50 deaths. raw_record.support_text: Ott et al [1977] studied 594 males exposed to benzene in three chemical production areas of a Michigan plant who began employment between 1940 and 1970. Three leukemia cases were observed, all myelocytic and two classified as acute myelocytic leukemia. These were significantly in excess of the expected number of 0.8 (p less than 0.047); all three cases were exposed to atmospheric benzene concentrations averaging less than 10 ppm.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: 594 male chemical production workers exposed to benzene (Ott et al, 1977)
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: All three leukemia cases were exposed to atmospheric benzene concentrations averaging less than 10 ppm.
raw_record.extra_details: Two of the three leukemia cases were acute myelocytic leukemia; one case was coded on the death certificate as bronchopneumonia, so expected cases were based on Third National Cancer Survey morbidity rather than mortality data; two deaths from anemia (one aplastic, one pernicious) were also observed. This finding prompted Dow Chemical Company [1977] to reduce benzene exposure globally to a 10 ppm ceiling.

raw_record.support_text: Infante et al [1977] reanalyzed data from a benzene-exposed worker cohort accounting for specific leukemia cell types. Of seven observed leukemia deaths, one was chronic myelogenous leukemia and six were acute myelogenous or monocytic leukemia. Against the expected number of 0.70 deaths from acute and monocytic leukemia, the six observed cases yielded an SMR of 857, representing a marked excess of acute myelogenous and monocytic leukemia associated with benzene exposure.
raw_record.extra_details: Six of seven benzene-related leukemia deaths were acute myelogenous/monocytic leukemia; SMR 857 versus expected 0.70 based on NCI mortality rates; expected counts included other cell types (e.g., acute lymphatic leukemia), making the SMR conservative. A 29-year-old cohort member dying of chronic myelogenous leukemia within 2 years of initial exposure was excluded from this analysis.

SIR for the whole cohort was 680.5 (95% CI 140.2-1988.5); for single-agent VP-16 subgroup SIR was 2270.0 (95% CI 275-8199), IR 14.7 per 1000 PYRs. Two cases published elsewhere [11, 12]. raw_record.support_text: Endometrial carcinoma has been observed in women treated with tamoxifen therapy. Swedish investigators reported a more than fivefold excess risk of endometrial carcinoma in women randomized to receive 40 mg of tamoxifen daily for either 2 or 5 years compared with controls. In the NSABP B-14 trial, researchers reported an absolute risk of tamoxifen-induced endometrial cancer of one to two cases annually per 1,000 women treated and a relative risk two to three times greater than in untreated women; 15 of 1,419 women randomized to 20 mg tamoxifen daily for 5 years developed endometrial cancer. The cumulative incidence of endometrial cancers in tamoxifen-treated women in major adjuvant trials was 0.9% versus 0.2% in controls.

NSABP B-14: 15/1,419 randomized and 8/1,220 nonrandomized treated patients developed endometrial cancer; 2/1,424 placebo recipients (later treated with tamoxifen). Dutch investigators reported a relative risk of 1.3; Danish investigators a nonsignificant threefold excess with 30 mg daily for 48 weeks. Risk increased with duration of use.

raw_record.support_text: To analyze the role of immunesurveillance in chemically induced lung tumorigenesis, 14-16-day-old T-cell-deficient BALB/c nude (nu/nu) mice and immunocompetent littermate BALB/c (nu/+) mice were given urethan (ethyl carbamate) intraperitoneally at 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, or 1.5 mg/g body weight and sacrificed 6 months later to count lung tumors. The dose-response for lung tumor induction was nearly identical between nu/nu and nu/+ mice. In the time-course study at 0.5 mg/g urethan, lung tumor incidence reached 73%/80% at 6 months and 96%/97% at 12 months in nu/nu and nu/+ groups, respectively, with mean lung tumor counts of 4.8 and 4.4 per mouse, indicating urethan induces lung adenomas/tumors in mice.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Intraperitoneal administration; 14-16-day-old mice; linear-quadratic dose-response and delayed time-course assessment; newer/newborn mice noted as more susceptible to urethan lung-adenoma induction.
raw_record.extra_details: Also reported: linear-quadratic tumorigenic response, no difference between T-cell-deficient nu/nu and nu/+ mice (no support for immunesurveillance mechanism); role of urethan metabolites and nucleic-acid adduct formation in tumorigenesis; related genes ptr, Pas-1/-2/-3 and H-2 (I-A/I-E) subregions proposed as lung tumor regulators.

raw_record.support_text: Progesterone (Pg) was evaluated to determine whether it alone could induce mammary tumors. Mice implanted s.c. with 40 mg Pg silastic pellets initially and a 20 mg Pg pellet 6 months later (total 60 mg) developed mammary tumors with an actuarial incidence of 28%. Pg induced mostly lobular, progestin-independent mammary tumors in BALB/c female mice.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: lobular carcinoma of the mammary gland
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Subcutaneous administration as silastic pellets (40 mg at start plus 20 mg at 6 months, total 60 mg); actuarial incidence 28%.
raw_record.extra_details: Pg-induced tumors were predominantly infiltrating lobular carcinomas (67%) with 33% ductal carcinomas; lobular tumors behaved as progestin-independent in syngeneic passages. Tumor latency about 46 weeks.

raw_record.extra_details: Aliases in text: cyclosporin. Cyclosporine also shortened the mean interval between transplantation and lymphoma from ~4 years to as little as 4 months. Acyclovir had little impact on survival, attributed to absence of viral replication in this context.

raw_record.support_text: The etoposide-associated secondary leukemia is described as a clinically and morphologically clearly characterized leukemia form, distinguished from leukemia after alkylating-agent chemotherapy by a shorter mean latency of 2-3 years, absence of a preleukemic phase, changes at chromosome 11q23, and predominantly myelomonocytic or monocytic differentiation. The leukemia risk appears markedly increased when a cumulative etoposide dose of 2 g/m² is exceeded and when etoposide is given one to two times weekly as maintenance therapy over a longer period.

raw_record.extra_details: Mean latency 2-3 years, no preleukemic phase, chromosome 11q23 abnormalities, myelomonocytic/monocytic differentiation; standard-dose risk below 1% based on three studies covering over 2000 patients; higher etoposide doses have insufficient data.

raw_record.extra_details: 5-12% cumulative risk of t-AML reported. Similar cumulative doses given every other week (ALL) or on a daily x4 schedule (non-Hodgkin's lymphoma) appeared to be associated with lower rates of t-AML. Germ cell patients treated with 1,500-2,500 mg/m² etoposide on a daily x5 schedule had a low risk of t-AML.

raw_record.support_text: Gabapentin-induced acinar cell tumors of the rat pancreas were reported to lack Ki-ras gene mutations. The sequences of the Ki-ras gene in pancreatic proliferative lesions induced by gabapentin after 2 years of administration to male Wistar rats at doses ~40-fold the maximum human dose were analyzed by PCR and direct sequencing, which confirmed the unaltered nucleotide sequences at codons 12, 13, and 61 in these adenomas or carcinomas of rat exocrine pancreas exposed to gabapentin.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: acinar cell tumors of the rat pancreas (adenomas and adenocarcinomas)
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: 2 years of administration to male Wistar rats at doses ~40-fold the maximum human dose
raw_record.extra_details: Induced acinar cell tumors lack Ki-ras gene mutations at codons 12 (GGT), 13 (GGC), and 61 (CAA); contrasted with human pancreatic exocrine tumors in which Ki-ras mutations are frequent. Analyzed retrospectively from formalin-fixed paraffin sections by PCR amplification of 110-base fragments and direct sequencing. Gabapentin is 1-(aminomethyl)cyclohexane-acetic acid.

Carcinogen (AFB1) dosing produced morphological changes characteristic of malignant neoplasms in liver tissues of animals killed 63 weeks after termination of dosing and beyond, and consistent preneoplastic lesions (increased mitotic activity, basophilia, hyperplasia) appeared from week 20 after termination of dosing.

raw_record.extra_details: 5% of patients developed bladder cancer; 31-fold increase vs general population and 51-fold for persons younger than 65 years. Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidence estimates: 2% at 5 years, 5% at 10 years, 16% at 15 years. Emphasized as a minimum estimate given the long latency between initiation of cyclophosphamide therapy and bladder cancer diagnosis. Microscopic nonglomerular hematuria was a significant risk factor and a sensitive marker for cyclophosphamide-induced bladder injury; cumulative dose exceeding 100 g (12% developed cancer) may emerge as an independent risk factor. Smoking history was not a statistically significant risk factor but smokers developed hematuria and bladder cancer after fewer months of treatment.

raw_record.support_text: The food-derived mutagenic heterocyclic aromatic amine 2-amino-3-methylimidazo[4,5-f]quinoline (IQ) is reported as a potent hepatocarcinogen in cynomolgus monkeys. In an ongoing carcinogenesis study, 34 of 40 monkeys dosed with IQ developed malignant liver tumors, the majority classified as hepatocellular carcinoma, with intrahepatic vascular invasion in 41.2% and metastases in 17.6% of HCC cases.
raw_record.extra_details: IQ is a food-derived mutagenic heterocyclic aromatic amine; 94 tumors and non-neoplastic lesions from 34 cases were examined; aberrant cytokeratin 7 expression observed in some HCC nodules.

raw_record.support_text: Long-term dosing of monkeys with IQ induced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with a range of biological behaviors. The passage describes IQ-induced HCC cases including well-differentiated, clear-cell, spindle-cell, hemorrhagic peloid, and poorly-differentiated variants, with intrahepatic vascular invasion and lung metastases, demonstrating that IQ dosing produced hepatocellular carcinoma tumors in the monkey liver.
raw_record.extra_details: IQ (2-amino-3-methylimidazo[4,5-f]quinoline)-induced tumors in monkey liver; tumors included well-differentiated, clear-cell, spindle-cell, hemorrhagic peloid, and poorly-differentiated variants; regression of primary tumors occurred in two cases with tumor-latent periods of 5.5 and 8 years; intrahepatic vascular invasion in 14/34 cases and lung metastases in 6/34 cases.

raw_record.support_text: The IPCS used chloroform mouse liver tumor data to calculate a tolerable daily intake value of 10 µg/kg body weight per day, using a no observed effect level of 10 mg/kg per day for cytolethality and cell proliferation in B6C3F1 female mice as input. In arriving at an acceptable exposure they applied an uncertainty factor of 1000, including ×10 for severity of effect, i.e., carcinogenicity. This treats chloroform as inducing liver carcinogenicity in B6C3F1 female mice.
raw_record.classification_label: carcinogen (treated as carcinogenic severity-of-effect in IPCS risk assessment)
raw_record.extra_details: IPCS risk assessment used mouse liver tumor data together with a NOEL of 10 mg/kg/day for cytolethality and cell proliferation; uncertainty factor of 1000 applied (×10 interspecies, ×10 intraspecies, ×10 for severity including carcinogenicity). IPCS made no body surface area correction because chloroform does not act by direct DNA damage and metabolism is similar in rodents and humans.

Malignant sarcomas developed at the injection site in the benzo[a]pyrene-treated animals within 100-120 days, and the accompanying rise in anti-phosphatidylinositol antibodies suggested that benzo[a]pyrene-stimulated neoplasia altered endogenous substance metabolism. The neoplasia is described as being stimulated by benzo[a]pyrene.

raw_record.support_text: Isoprene exposure in B6C3F1 mice induced Harderian gland neoplasms, with tumor incidences of 13/30 at 2200 ppm and 12/30 at 7000 ppm. The text states that isoprene exerts its carcinogenic activity, in part, by promoting spontaneously initiated cells (a promotional effect), and that both K-ras codon 61 CTA and H-ras codon 61 AAA mutations contribute to the isoprene carcinogenic process in the Harderian gland.
raw_record.extra_details: A high frequency of A→T transversions was found at H-ras codon 61 (AAA) as evidence of a direct mutagenic effect; the increase in H-ras codon 61 AAA mutations, especially at high exposure, supports a promotional effect on background H-ras mutations. The proportion of K-ras codon 61 CTA mutations was twice as high at 2200 ppm than at 7000 ppm, indicating different molecular mechanisms of isoprene carcinogenesis at high and lower doses. Genotoxic endpoints (SCE in bone marrow, micronucleated erythrocytes) showed a plateau at increasing concentrations, suggesting saturation of isoprene metabolism.

raw_record.support_text: Fifteen male workers exposed to vinyl chloride developed angiosarcoma of the liver; thirteen died of disease. Exposure time ranged from 4 to 27.8 years (average 16.9 years). The paper states that reduction of industrial chemical exposure has already been achieved and will hopefully eliminate this chemically related tumor in the future, linking vinyl chloride exposure in the PVC plant workers to the hepatic angiosarcomas.

raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Occupational exposure to gaseous vinyl chloride during PVC production; 15 cases observed (8 in Louisville, Kentucky and 7 in Shawinigan, Quebec).
raw_record.extra_details: Patients aged 36 to 58 years (average 47.5). Liver gross features included hemorrhagic necrosis, cystic degeneration, fibrosis, and apparent multicentricity; subcapsular fibrosis, portal fibrosis, and endothelial cell hyperplasia were noted. Two of eight autopsied patients had distant organ involvement, one duodenal. No proven cases of angiosarcoma were reported among workers not exposed to gaseous vinyl chloride.

raw_record.support_text: Isotopic and angiographic studies of hepatic angiosarcoma in vinyl chloride workers are presented. The liver scan has been the most useful screening procedure in detecting the tumor, and subcapsular fibrosis, portal fibrosis, sinusoidal dilatation and endothelial lining cell hyperplasia are associated with the tumors. Follow-up studies will assess whether these changes are reversible after removal of these men from vinyl chloride exposure.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Occupational setting (vinyl chloride monomer production workers); findings based on a screened case series.
raw_record.extra_details: Screening study of hepatic angiosarcoma in exposed workers; liver scan most useful for detection. Associated non-neoplastic hepatic lesions include subcapsular fibrosis, portal fibrosis, sinusoidal dilatation, and endothelial lining cell hyperplasia. Wedged hepatic venography created iatrogenic hepatic infarcts resembling angiosarcoma, leading to a right hepatic lobectomy in one case.

raw_record.support_text: In 15 polyvinyl chloride (PVC) polymerization workers who developed hepatic angiosarcoma, the paper attributes the tumors to vinyl chloride monomer exposure, stating that 'the vinyl chloride monomer-induced cases occur at a relatively early age for this type of tumor' and suggesting that, once started, the carcinogenic process may not always be reversible with removal from the monomer exposure. It notes that even a relatively brief 4-year exposure could be significant for developing the tumor 15 years later.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Occupational exposure in PVC polymerization plant workers; long latency (12-29 years from initial work to diagnosis).
raw_record.extra_details: Cases at Louisville (KY), Niagara Falls (NY), South Charleston (WV), and Pottstown (PA) plants. Most were initially misdiagnosed as hepatoma or cirrhosis. Many workers had begun work in the 1940s-early 1950s when highest monomer exposure levels were presumed, but Patient 7 began work in 1962, indicating risk factors still present in the early 1960s. Spontaneous hepatic angiosarcomas typically occur in older age groups, whereas monomer-induced cases occurred at a relatively early age.

raw_record.support_text: In rats, chronic administration of lacidipine suppresses testosterone production, keeping plasma LH levels high and continuously stimulating Leydig cells, which activates PKC, up-regulates LHRH receptors, and eventually 'finally leads to tumor development.' The passage refers to 'lacidipine-induced LCTs in rats,' indicating that lacidipine produces Leydig cell tumors in rats, supported by results from a 78-week treatment study showing down-regulation of LH receptors, up-regulation of LHRH receptors, and increased PKC activity, proto-oncoprotein expression, and DNA content in isolated Leydig cells.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Chronic administration for 78 weeks in rats
raw_record.extra_details: Proposed mechanism: Ca-blocking action inhibits Ca influx, suppressing testosterone production; resultant feedback increases plasma LH, down-regulates LH receptors and up-regulates LHRH receptors, activating protein kinase C (PKC) and prompting c-ras and cell cycle-regulating gene expression and Leydig cell proliferation. Testosterone production decreased while PKC activity and BrdU uptake increased. LHRH receptor signaling is highlighted as key to LCT induction.

raw_record.extra_details: DMBA is described as a well-known carcinogen in the field of experimental tumor production. Palpable ovarian neoplasms developed in 19 of 40 rats between weeks 19 and 36; 17 epithelial and 2 nonepithelial neoplasms. All tumors were malignant (none benign or borderline); extraovarian spread to the peritoneal surface occurred in 7 rats, 3 with bloody ascites. Histologic subtyping included serous, endometrioid, hobnail cell, mixed, and sarcomatous tumors; two adenocarcinomas showed squamous cell transformation. DMBA (Wako) was heated to its fusion point (~124°C), ~2.1 µg per suture. DMBA also referred to as 7,12-Dimethylbenz[a]anthracene.

raw_record.support_text: The paper states that among the carcinogens in cigarette smoke, the nitrosamines, especially N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA), are kidney carcinogens in rodents. A separate abstract statement notes that carcinogens in cigarette smoke, especially nitrosamines, induce kidney tumors of a variety of histologic types in rodents. The study's own model is described: intraperitoneal injection of NDMA into protein-deprived female Wistar rats induced renal-tubule-derived epithelial tumors in up to 90% of dosed rats, mostly of granular cell type with about 10% clear or mixed clear/granular cell type.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: Renal (kidney) epithelial tumors of the renal tubules (granular, clear, or mixed clear/granular cell type)
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: High-incidence model requiring a prior 3–5 day protein-deprivation diet (glucose:sucrose with glucose drinking water) to reduce hepatic NDMA metabolism and increase dose delivery to the kidneys; one or two intraperitoneal injections of NDMA at 30 mg/kg body weight.
raw_record.extra_details: NDMA is one of the nitrosamine carcinogens present in cigarette smoke. The induced renal epithelial tumors were histologically similar to human clear cell renal cell carcinomas. Four VHL gene mutations (three G:C to A:T and one A:T to G:C) were found in three of eight clear or mixed clear/granular tumors, versus none in 40 previously reported rat kidney tumors of other histologic types (P = .003), reported as the first VHL mutations in kidney tumors after direct chemical exposure.

raw_record.support_text: Rats dosed with AFB1 daily for 5 weeks developed hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); total HCC incidence dropped significantly from 83% to 60% and 48% in the delayed-transient and persistent oltipraz intervention groups versus no intervention, and there was a significant association between integrated serum aflatoxin-albumin adduct level and risk of HCC (P=0.01). Reduction in biomarker levels reflected protection against carcinogenesis, but adduct levels could not identify individuals destined to develop HCC.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: AFB1 dosed daily for 5 weeks; HCC incidence 83% baseline with no intervention, reduced by oltipraz chemoprevention.
raw_record.extra_details: HCC risk was significantly associated with integrated aflatoxin-albumin serum adduct level (P=0.01) at the population level but showed no predictive value for individual risk (P=0.56).

condition_group: model=starved nzr/gd rat+reported_condition=single i.p. dose of 20 mg/kg in starved nzr/gd rats; origin from the lining of the nasal cavity (dorsal angular regions and upper septum)+route=injection_or_parenteral+species=rat
condition_text: Single i.p. dose of 20 mg/kg in starved NZR/Gd rats; origin from the lining of the nasal cavity (dorsal angular regions and upper septum)

raw_record.support_text: Nasal cavity tumors presented as masses distorting the nasal bones, with larger tumors being well differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinomas and a few predominantly anaplastic, eroding and invading nasal orbital and cranial cavities. The results confirm the efficacy of DMN as a carcinogenic stimulus for nasal cavity epithelium. Induction of nasal cavity tumors by i.p. injection of DMN was described as an example of organotropic effect of the N-nitrosamines.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: nasal cavity tumors (keratinizing squamous cell carcinomas, some anaplastic)
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Single i.p. dose of 20 mg/kg in starved NZR/Gd rats; origin from the lining of the nasal cavity (dorsal angular regions and upper septum)
raw_record.extra_details: N-nitrosamines had previously been reported to induce malignant nasal cavity tumors in rats by inhalation or i.v. injection; no neuroepitheliomas were induced in this experiment.

condition_text: perinatal (about 2 weeks of age) DEN injection; male mice only

raw_record.support_text: Perinatally DEN-initiated hepatocarcinogenesis in male mice produces hepatic tumors that are mostly hepatocellular adenomas, with carcinomas also observed occasionally; male C3H/HeJ mice are about 50 times more susceptible than male C57BL/6J mice.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: perinatal (about 2 weeks of age) DEN injection; male mice only
raw_record.extra_details: C3H/HeJ ~50-fold more susceptible than C57BL/6J; susceptibility controlled by Hcs genes; induction is a mutational initiation event attributed to DNA adduct formation.
